exercises.name: 3/4 Sit-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, hands behind your head. 2. Engage your core and lift your shoulders about three-quarters of the way up toward your knees. 3. Pause briefly, then lower back down with control. Keep your neck neutral—don't pull your head forward.

exercises.name: Ab Crunch Machine
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in the machine with your chest against the pad and hands on the handles. 2. Pull the handles down by contracting your abs, bringing your ribs toward your hips. 3. Release slowly back to start. Avoid jerking—use a smooth, controlled movement.

exercises.name: Ab Roller
exercises.instructions: 1. Kneel on the ground holding the roller handles with straight arms. 2. Roll forward, extending your body into a plank-like position, engaging your abs. 3. Roll back to start by pulling with your core. Keep your spine neutral throughout—don't let your lower back sag.

exercises.name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with the kettlebell overhead in one hand, arm straight and locked. 2. Drop your hips and rotate your torso, lowering your opposite hand toward the ground while tracking the bell overhead. 3. Return to standing. This advanced move demands core stability and shoulder control.

exercises.name: Air Bike
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back, knees bent 90 degrees, hands behind your head. 2. Bring your opposite elbow to knee, extending the other leg, then alternate in a pedaling motion. 3. Keep your core tight and move fluidly without jerking. Your neck stays neutral throughout.

exercises.name: Alternate Hammer Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing inward (hammer grip). 2. Curl one dumbbell up toward your shoulder while keeping the other arm still. 3. Lower and repeat on the other side. Keep your elbows locked at your sides—don't swing the weight.

exercises.name: Alternate Heel Touchers
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor, arms at your sides. 2. Crunch up slightly and reach your right hand toward your right heel, then return. 3. Repeat on the left side in a controlled, alternating rhythm. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.

exercises.name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on an incline bench set to 45 degrees, holding dumbbells with palms forward. 2. Curl one dumbbell toward your shoulder, pause, then lower. 3. Repeat on the opposite side. The incline prevents momentum—keep your back flat against the bench.

exercises.name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from the cable machine with handles at shoulder height. 2. Press one handle forward and up, fully extending your arm. 3. Return and repeat on the other side. Maintain an upright posture and avoid arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs. 2. Raise one dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height with a slight bend in your elbow. 3. Lower and repeat on the other side. Use controlled, smooth motions—don't jerk the weight up.

exercises.name: Alternating Floor Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back holding kettlebells at chest level. 2. Press one kettlebell up toward the ceiling, fully extending your arm. 3. Lower back to chest and repeat on the other side. Keep your shoulders packed and core braced throughout.

exercises.name: Alternating Hang Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a kettlebell by the handle at waist height, hinging slightly at the hips. 2. Explosively extend your hips and knees, pulling the kettlebell upward and into the rack position at your shoulder. 3. Lower back down and repeat on the opposite arm. The power comes from your hips and hamstrings, not your arms.

exercises.name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding kettlebells at shoulder height in the rack position. 2. Press one kettlebell overhead while keeping the other stable at shoulder height. 3. Lower and press the opposite side. Your core braced and glutes engaged keep you stable—don't let your torso shift.

exercises.name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend forward with a flat back, holding a kettlebell in each hand at knee level. 2. Pull one kettlebell up to your hip, squeezing your upper back. 3. Lower and row the other side. Keep your hips level—avoid twisting your torso.

exercises.name: Alternating Renegade Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Get into a plank position with hands on two kettlebells. 2. Pull one kettlebell up to your hip while stabilizing with the other arm. 3. Lower and row the opposite side. Your core tight and hips level maintain proper alignment—don't rotate.

exercises.name: Anti-Gravity Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on an incline bench holding a barbell at chest height. 2. Press the bar up and away from your body, stopping just short of full lockout. 3. Lower back to chest. This variation reduces momentum—focus on a controlled squeeze through your shoulders and chest.

exercises.name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing your body. 2. Press up while rotating your wrists so palms face forward at the top. 3. Lower while rotating palms back to face you. This rotation engages more of your shoulder from multiple angles.

exercises.name: Around The Worlds
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell horizontally with both hands at chest level. 2. Raise and circle the dumbbell around your head, making a full rotation. 3. Complete your reps in one direction, then reverse. Keep your chest engaged and core tight throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Trainer
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself over a rounded stone on a platform, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Hug the stone and explosively extend your hips and knees to pull it toward your body. 3. Stand up and lower back down. This heavy, full-body lift demands perfect hip drive—keep your back flat.

exercises.name: Atlas Stones
exercises.instructions: 1. Straddle a heavy stone on the ground with feet wide. 2. Wrap your arms around it, explosively extend your hips and knees to lift it to your lap. 3. Stand and place it on the next platform. This strongman movement recruits your entire posterior chain.

exercises.name: Axle Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with the thick axle bar over mid-foot, shoulders over the bar. 2. Pull by driving your knees forward and hips up, keeping the bar close. 3. Lower with control, keeping your back neutral. The thicker grip demands full-body tension—don't relax your lats.

exercises.name: Back Flyes - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing an anchor point with a resistance band. 2. With arms extended at shoulder height, pull the band apart by moving your arms back and out. 3. Return slowly. The band's constant tension fires your rear delts throughout—maintain a slight bend in your elbows.

exercises.name: Backward Drag
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach weight to a sled or harness, then face away and walk backward pulling the load. 2. Take controlled steps, maintaining an upright posture. 3. Finish the distance. This unilateral focus builds quad endurance and core stability.

exercises.name: Balance Board
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand on a balance board with feet hip-width apart. 2. Rise up onto your toes, holding the position while maintaining balance. 3. Lower your heels back down. Engage your calves and stabilizer muscles—keep your core tight for balance.

exercises.name: Ball Leg Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball, legs extended. 2. Bend your knees and roll the ball toward your glutes by engaging your hamstrings. 3. Extend back out. Your hips stay elevated—don't let them sag as you curl.

exercises.name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip the pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart and place your knees or feet in a resistance band for assistance. 2. Pull yourself up by driving your elbows back and down. 3. Lower with control. The band assists you—still engage your lats fully.

exercises.name: Band Good Morning
exercises.instructions: 1. Place a resistance band over your shoulders and hold it with both hands. 2. Hinge at the hips, moving your torso forward while keeping your back straight. 3. Return to standing. Your hamstrings and lower back contract—keep your knees slightly bent and core braced.

exercises.name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with a resistance band looped low around a post behind you. 2. Hinge forward at your hips, letting the band pull through your legs. 3. Drive your hips forward to stand. This posterior chain move emphasizes hip extension—stay upright.

exercises.name: Band Hip Adductions
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with a resistance band around both thighs just above your knees. 2. Step sideways with control, creating tension in the band. 3. Bring your feet together. Your quads and inner thighs work to pull against the band's resistance.

exercises.name: Band Pull Apart
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a resistance band at shoulder height with arms extended in front of you. 2. Pull the band apart by moving your arms out and back, stretching your arms wide. 3. Return with control. This isolation move targets your rear delts and improves shoulder health—use a light band.

exercises.name: Band Skull Crusher
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a resistance band looped over a high anchor, facing away, hands at head level. 2. Extend your arms forward and down, straightening your elbows. 3. Bend back to the starting position. Keep your upper arms still—only your forearms move.

exercises.name: Barbell Ab Rollout
exercises.instructions:
Place a barbell on the floor at your feet.
Bending at the waist, grip the barbell with a shoulder with overhand grip.
With a slow controlled motion, roll the bar out so that your back is straight.
Roll back up raising your hips and butt as you return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees
exercises.instructions: 1. Kneel holding the barbell with shoulders over the bar, arms straight. 2. Roll the bar forward, extending your body into a long line. 3. Pull the bar back to start using your abs. Keep your core tight—don't let your hips sink.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip
exercises.instructions:
Lay down on a bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.
If you train with a high weight it is advisable to have a spotter that can help you up if you can't lift the weight on your own.
With the width of the grip you can also control which part of the chest is trained more:
wide grip: outer chest muscles
narrow grip: inner chest muscles and triceps

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at hip height, hands shoulder-width apart, palms forward. 2. Bend your elbows and curl the bar up toward your chest. 3. Lower back down. Keep your elbows fixed at your sides—don't swing to generate momentum.

exercises.name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on an incline bench leaning back, holding a barbell at hip height with palms forward. 2. Curl the bar up toward your chest by bending your elbows. 3. Lower back down. The incline eliminates swing—your biceps work in isolation.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with the bar over mid-foot, shoulders over the bar, back flat. 2. Drive your knees forward and hips up, pulling the bar in a straight line. 3. Lock out at the top, then lower with control. This full-body lift starts with your lats engaged—don't let the bar drift away.

exercises.name: Barbell Full Squat
exercises.instructions:
The barbell full squat is a compound exercise that targets multiple muscle groups in the lower body, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes.
Proper form is crucial for maximizing results and preventing injuries during the barbell full squat. This includes maintaining a shoulder-width stance, creating whole body tension, controlling your descent, and maintaining proper depth and knee positioning.
Assistance moves such as the front squat, goblet squat, split squat, and Bulgarian split squat can help improve your performance in the barbell full squat by targeting specific muscle groups and improving overall technique.
To achieve new personal records in your back squat, gradually increase weight over time, vary rep ranges and sets to stimulate muscle growth, and prioritize rest and recovery between training sessions.

exercises.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on the ground with a barbell across your hips, upper back against a bench. 2. Drive your hips up, squeezing your glutes hard at the top. 3. Lower back down. Focus on glute contraction—don't push through your knees.

exercises.name: Barbell Guillotine Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench with the barbell at neck height, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. 2. Press the bar up and away from your body. 3. Lower to neck height. This upper-chest focus move requires controlled depth—don't use heavy weight until you master form.

exercises.name: Barbell Hack Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Squat against a leg press machine or hack squat frame, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Lower your hips until your knees reach 90 degrees. 3. Drive through your heels to stand. This quad-dominant squat variant keeps your torso upright—don't let your knees cave inward.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.instructions: The bar should go directly on your upper thigh, directly below your crotch. Your feet should be directly under your knees. Push your hips up so that you form a straight line from your knees to your shoulders. Use a pad for comfort.

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on an incline bench set to 30–45 degrees, holding the barbell at mid-chest with a medium grip. 2. Press the bar up and slightly forward. 3. Lower with control. Your upper chest and front delts are working hard—maintain steady breathing.

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie face-down on an incline bench holding a barbell, arms extended forward. 2. Raise the barbell up and back over your head using your shoulders. 3. Lower back down. This unusual angle isolates your shoulders—move slowly and deliberately.

exercises.name: Barbell Lunge
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell on your shoulders and step forward with one leg, lowering until both knees bend 90 degrees. 2. Push through your front heel to return to standing. 3. Repeat on the other side. Keep your torso upright and front knee tracking over your toe.

exercises.name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Hinge forward at the hips with the barbell at hip height, arms extended, back flat. 2. Row the barbell up toward your lower chest, leading with your elbows. 3. Lower back down. Your rear delts and upper back contract—use a light weight to focus on form.

exercises.name: Barbell Rollout from Bench
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a bench holding a barbell, then bend and place your hands on the bar. 2. Roll the bar forward, extending your body into a plank. 3. Roll back to the bench using your abs. Core engagement is essential—don't let your lower back sag.

exercises.name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench with a barbell resting on your thighs just above your knees. 2. Rise up on your toes, lifting the barbell. 3. Lower your heels back down. Pause at the top to squeeze your calves—this isolates the soleus muscle.

exercises.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: Sit on a bench, the back rest should be almost vertical. Take a barbell with a shoulder wide grip and bring it up to chest height. Press the weight up, but don't stretch the arms completely. Go slowly down and repeat.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at hip height with a neutral grip, arms straight. 2. Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, driving them as high as possible. 3. Lower back down. Focus on shoulder elevation—your traps do the work.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with a barbell held behind your back at hip height. 2. Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears. 3. Lower back down. This variation changes the angle—your traps engage differently than front shrugs.

exercises.name: Barbell Side Bend
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell across your shoulders or at your side, standing upright. 2. Bend your torso laterally, moving your torso to one side. 3. Return to upright and repeat on the other side. Your obliques and lateral abs contract—avoid forward rounding.

exercises.name: Barbell Side Split Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell on your shoulders, then step to one side into a deep squat, keeping the other leg straight. 2. Drive through your front heel to return to standing. 3. Repeat on the other side. This unilateral move builds single-leg strength—keep your torso upright.

exercises.name: Barbell Squat
exercises.instructions: Place a barbell in a rack just below shoulder-height. Dip under the bar to put it behind the neck across the top of the back, and grip the bar with the hands wider than shoulder-width apart. Lift the chest up and squeeze the shoulder blades together to keep the straight back throughout the entire movement. Stand up to bring the bar off the rack and step backwards, then place the feet so that they are a little wider than shoulder-width apart. Sit back into hips and keep the back straight and the chest up, squatting down so the hips are below the knees. From the bottom of the squat, press feet into the ground and push hips forward to return to the top of the standing position.

exercises.name: Barbell Squat To A Bench
exercises.instructions: 1. Load a barbell on your shoulders and squat until you lightly tap a bench behind you. 2. Immediately drive back up through your heels. 3. Repeat. Touching the bench ensures consistent depth—drive through your whole foot.

exercises.name: Barbell Step Ups
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a step or platform holding a barbell on your shoulders. 2. Step up with one leg, driving through your front heel to stand on the step. 3. Step back down. Repeat on the other leg. This single-leg movement builds quad and glute strength.

exercises.name: Barbell Walking Lunge
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell on your shoulders and take a large step forward, lowering your hips until both knees bend 90 degrees. 2. Push through your front heel and step forward into the next lunge. 3. Continue walking and lunging. Maintain an upright posture throughout—don't let your torso lean.

exercises.name: Battling Ropes
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a wall holding heavy ropes, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Move your arms up and down explosively, creating waves in the ropes. 3. Keep moving for time or distance. Your delts and core stabilize your body—maintain an athletic stance.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl Sled Drags
exercises.instructions: 1. Get into a bear crawl position with a sled harness attached. 2. Move forward on your hands and feet in a crawling motion, dragging the sled. 3. Continue for distance. This full-body move demands core stability and quad endurance.

exercises.name: Bench Dips
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip a bench behind you with straight arms, legs extended forward (add weight with a plate on your lap if needed). 2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until they reach 90 degrees. 3. Press back up. Keep your elbows tucked—flaring them out shifts work to your shoulders.

exercises.name: Bench Press - Powerlifting
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench, bar at mid-chest, shoulder blades retracted. 2. Lower the bar to your chest, then press up powerfully. 3. Lock out fully at the top. A wide, powerlifting grip emphasizes your triceps—keep the bar path straight.

exercises.name: Bench Press - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a bench with band resistance added to the barbell for accommodating resistance. 2. Lower the bar to your chest, then press upward. 3. Lockout at the top. The band increases resistance at the top—maximize that peak tension.

exercises.name: Bench Press with Chains
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a bench with chains draped over the bar for accommodating resistance. 2. Lower the bar to your chest. 3. Press up; more chain lifts off the ground as you ascend, increasing resistance. This teaches explosive power—bar speed accelerates.

exercises.name: Bent Over Barbell Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Hinge forward at your hips with the barbell at knee level, keeping your back flat. 2. Pull the bar up toward your lower chest, driving your elbows back and up. 3. Lower with control. Your traps and lats contract—keep the bar path close to your body.

exercises.name: Bent Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie face-down on an incline bench with your chest against it, holding dumbbells. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides, leading with your elbows. 3. Lower back down. The bench support removes momentum—your rear delts work in true isolation.

exercises.name: Bent Over Low-Pulley Side Lateral
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend forward to 45 degrees, holding a cable handle at knee level with one arm. 2. Raise the cable out to your side to shoulder height, leading with your elbow. 3. Lower and repeat. This side lateral targets your middle delt from a unique angle—avoid rounding your back.

exercises.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Load a barbell and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding one end with both hands. 2. Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, letting the bar hang at arm's length. 3. Pull the bar upward toward your ribs, driving your elbow back to engage your traps, then lower with control. Keep your spine neutral and core tight throughout.

exercises.name: Bent Over Two-Arm Long Bar Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, gripping a barbell at chest width with an overhand grip. 2. Bend forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the ground, arms extended with the bar hanging. 3. Drive your elbows back and pull the barbell toward your lower chest, squeezing your traps at the top. 4. Lower the bar under control without rounding your lower back.

exercises.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and bend forward at the hips so your torso is nearly horizontal, arms hanging straight down. 2. Pull both dumbbells upward by driving your elbows back, lifting them to your ribs. 3. Squeeze your traps at the top, then lower the weights with control. Keep your chest up and core engaged to prevent lower back strain.

exercises.name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row With Palms In
exercises.instructions: 1. Grab a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and hinge forward until your torso nearly touches your thighs. 2. Pull the dumbbells upward beside your body, focusing on driving your elbows back and up. 3. Pause at the top while squeezing your traps, then lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid twisting.

exercises.name: Bent Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Clean a kettlebell to shoulder height, then step back slightly with one leg for balance. 2. Press the kettlebell overhead by punching straight up while your torso leans back slightly and your working-side glute flexes. 3. As the bell rises, rotate your ribcage toward the weight to engage your core and abs. 4. Lower under control and reset before the next rep.

exercises.name: Bent-Arm Barbell Pullover
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie perpendicular across a bench with only your upper back supported, feet on the floor. 2. Hold a barbell with elbows slightly bent over your chest, then lower it in an arc behind your head, feeling a stretch in your lats and chest. 3. Pull the bar back over your chest, keeping the elbow bend constant. Keep your hips low and core braced.

exercises.name: Bent-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie perpendicular across a bench with your upper back supported, feet planted on the floor. 2. Hold a dumbbell above your chest with slightly bent elbows, then pull it upward and over your head in an arc. 3. Lower the weight behind and slightly below shoulder height, stretching your chest. 4. Pull the dumbbell back over your chest in a controlled arc.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Hip Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms at your sides. 2. Push through your feet and lift your hips upward, driving them toward the ceiling to engage your abs. 3. Pause briefly at the top while keeping your knees bent at 90 degrees, then lower your hips back down. 4. Avoid pulling on your neck or using momentum.

exercises.name: Bicycling
exercises.instructions: 1. Start on a stationary bike or outdoor bicycle at a comfortable pace to warm up. 2. Maintain steady pedaling with moderate resistance, aiming for a conversational breathing rate to build aerobic endurance in your quads. 3. Keep your posture upright or slightly forward depending on the bike setup, engaging your core. 4. Gradually adjust resistance and pace based on your fitness level and goals.

exercises.name: Bicycling, Stationary
exercises.instructions: 1. Adjust the seat height so your leg reaches near-full extension at the bottom of the pedal stroke on a stationary bike. 2. Begin pedaling at a moderate pace and resistance that allows steady breathing without stopping. 3. Maintain an upright posture with hands on the bars, knees tracking over your toes throughout the motion. 4. Build endurance in your quads by sustaining the effort for your target duration.

exercises.name: Board Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up on a bench with a barbell and a wooden board across your chest. 2. Unrack the barbell and lower it to touch the board (reducing range of motion), then press it upward to lockout. 3. Keep your feet flat and drive through your heels, maintaining a stable upper back against the bench. 4. Lower with control and repeat, using this partial range to overload your triceps.

exercises.name: Body Tricep Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench or the floor with your hands behind you, fingers pointing forward, legs extended in front. 2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are nearly parallel to the floor. 3. Press through your hands to raise your body back up, engaging your triceps at the top. Keep your shoulders away from your ears and core engaged.

exercises.name: Body-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright with your hands behind you on the edge of a bench, feet flat on the floor in front of you. 2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the ground. 3. Press back up to the starting position, leading with your triceps. Keep your shoulders pulled back and away from your ears throughout.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Flyes
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with a wide grip at chest height. 2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and open your arms out to the sides in a controlled arc, feeling a stretch across your chest. 3. Bring the bar back to the center in a reverse motion, squeezing your chest muscles together. Maintain the fixed elbow bend throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Mid Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip a suspension trainer or low bar with a neutral grip, body extended in front with heels on the ground. 2. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows back, squeezing your traps and back muscles. 3. Lower yourself back to the starting position under control. Keep your body straight and core braced.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward, arms relaxed at your sides or crossed on your chest. 2. Bend your knees and hips simultaneously, lowering into a squat until your thighs are parallel to the floor or lower. 3. Push through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your quads at the top. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Walking Lunge
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, hands on your hips or clasped in front of you. 2. Step forward with one leg and lower your body by bending both knees until your rear knee nearly touches the ground. 3. Push off your front foot and step forward into the next lunge with your other leg. Keep your torso upright and knees tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a stability dome facing a cable machine, holding a rope attachment behind your head. 2. Crunch forward, flexing your abs and bringing your elbows toward your hips. 3. Return to upright, then bend your torso to one side to work your obliques. 4. Alternate sides each rep, keeping your balance steady.

exercises.name: Bottoms Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, arms at your sides, palms down for support. 2. Press through your feet and hands to lift your glutes and lower back off the ground, bringing your knees toward your chest. 3. Lower your hips back to the starting position. Keep your neck neutral and abs engaged throughout.

exercises.name: Bottoms-Up Clean From The Hang Position
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell at your side with an overhand grip, bell hanging down. 2. Hinge at the hips slightly to load your hamstrings, then explosively extend your hips and pull the kettlebell upward. 3. Flip your wrist to catch the bell in an upright position at shoulder height, engaging your forearms. 4. Lower and repeat, focusing on a smooth flip rather than a jerky catch.

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.instructions:
Set up the box: Position the box behind you, about 3 feet from a squat rack if you're using a barbell. Choose a height that allows you to squat down and gently tap your glutes on the box with your back straight.
Stand with proper form: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward. Engage your core and keep your back neutral. If using a barbell, rack it at shoulder height.
Lower down: Sit back as if going to sit on a chair, bending your knees and lowering your hips towards the box. Keep your core tight and back straight throughout the movement.
Controlled descent: Descend in a controlled manner until your glutes gently touch the box. Don't plop down.
Pause and press up: Briefly pause at the bottom with your back straight and core engaged. Then, press through your heels to drive yourself back up to the starting position.
Improvements in coordination, balance and endurance, toning of the leg and buttock muscles and an overall increase in bone density eliminating the risk of osteoporosis.

exercises.name: Box Squat with Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up with a barbell across your shoulders, positioned over a box, with bands looped around the bar and anchored to the floor. 2. Squat down and lightly tap the box with your glutes, allowing the bands to assist as you rise. 3. Drive through your heels and extend your knees and hips to stand, with band resistance increasing as you rise. Keep your chest up and core braced.

exercises.name: Box Squat with Chains
exercises.instructions: 1. Rest a barbell on your shoulders with chains hung so they touch the ground at the bottom. 2. Squat down and lightly sit onto a box behind you, letting the chains slacken. 3. Drive up off the box through your heels as the chains lift and add resistance near the top. Keep your torso upright throughout.

exercises.name: Bradford/Rocky Presses
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell at shoulder height with feet shoulder-width apart and core engaged. 2. Press the barbell forward and slightly upward, then lower it behind your head to the rear shoulders. 3. Press the barbell back to the front position. Perform all reps in this front-to-back motion, working your shoulders through multiple planes.

exercises.name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned hip-width apart about six inches from your glutes. 2. Press through your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. 3. Hold the top position for a moment, feeling the glute contraction. 4. Lower your hips under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Butt-Ups
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat near your glutes, and arms at your sides with palms down. 2. Explosively drive through your feet to lift your hips and glutes high off the ground, bringing your knees up toward your chest. 3. Lower under control and repeat, maintaining momentum with your abs driving the movement. Keep your upper back on the ground.

exercises.name: Butterfly
exercises.instructions: Sit on the butterfly machine, the feet have a good contact with the floor, the upper arms are parallel to the floor. Press your arms together till the handles are practically together (but aren't!). Go slowly back. The weights should stay all the time in the air.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from a cable machine with handles at chest height, feet staggered for stability. 2. Press the handles forward and slightly upward, extending your arms fully while engaging your chest. 3. Bring the handles back toward your chest in a controlled manner, resisting the cable tension. Keep your core tight and avoid arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Cable Crossover
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in the center of a cable machine with both arms extended out to your sides, holding handles from high pulleys. 2. Bring both handles forward and across your body in a wide arc, squeezing your chest at the center point. 3. Return to the starting position with control. Maintain a slight forward lean and keep your arms mostly straight.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Kneel facing a cable stack with a rope attachment at head height, holding the rope behind your head with elbows bent. 2. Crunch downward by flexing your abs and driving your elbows toward your hips, rounding your upper back. 3. Return to the starting position under control without letting your lower back take over. Feel the squeeze in your abs at the bottom.

exercises.name: Cable Deadlifts
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with the handle at ground level, feet hip-width apart. 2. Grip the handle and hinge at the hips, lowering your torso while keeping your legs relatively straight. 3. Drive through your heels and extend your hips to stand upright, pulling the handle toward you. Keep your back neutral and core engaged.

exercises.name: Cable Hammer Curls - Rope Attachment
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable stack with a rope attachment at waist height, holding each end of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). 2. Curl the rope upward by bending your elbows, keeping them stationary at your sides. 3. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the rope with control. Avoid swinging or using momentum.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand sideways to a cable machine with the ankle strap attached to the inner ankle of your far leg. 2. Pull your leg across your body toward the center line, engaging your inner thigh muscles. 3. Control the return to the starting position against cable tension. Keep your torso upright throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Incline Pushdown
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach a straight bar to a high cable pulley and set an incline bench in front of it. 2. Sit on the incline with the bar at arm's length overhead, elbows slightly bent. 3. Press the bar downward by extending your arms, engaging your lats and upper back. Lower under control back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Cable Incline Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Set an incline bench in front of a cable stack and sit back against it, holding a rope attachment at head height. 2. Lower the rope toward your forehead by bending your elbows, feeling the stretch in your triceps. 3. Extend your arms upward and backward, bringing the rope overhead and behind your head. Squeeze your triceps at full extension.

exercises.name: Cable Internal Rotation
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand sideways to a cable machine with elbow bent 90 degrees, upper arm parallel to the floor, holding a handle at waist height. 2. Rotate your arm inward, bringing your forearm across your body while keeping your elbow stationary. 3. Return to the starting position under control. Perform all reps on one side, then switch, working your shoulder rotators.

exercises.name: Cable Iron Cross
exercises.instructions: 1. Set both cable pulleys to shoulder height and stand centered between them, holding a handle in each hand with arms out to your sides. 2. With a slight elbow bend, sweep both handles forward and cross them in front of your chest. 3. Open back out to the sides with control, feeling the stretch across your chest.

exercises.name: Cable Judo Flip
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in front of a cable machine with a handle positioned at waist height, holding it with both hands. 2. Explosively rotate your torso and flip the cable across your body in a dynamic twisting motion, engaging your core and abs. 3. Control the return and reverse direction, alternating sides with each repetition. Maintain an athletic stance throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench with a cable handle held above your chest, elbows bent to about 90 degrees. 2. Lower the cable by bending your elbows, bringing the handle toward your forehead or behind the top of your head. 3. Extend your arms upward to return to the starting position, squeezing your triceps. Keep your elbows stationary and core engaged.

exercises.name: Cable One Arm Tricep Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from a cable machine, holding a handle at shoulder height with one hand, elbow bent. 2. Extend your arm upward and backward, pressing the handle overhead in a controlled manner. 3. Lower the handle back to shoulder height by bending your elbow. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Cable Preacher Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a preacher curl bench and position a cable handle attachment so the pulley is at the height of the bend in the pad. 2. Rest your upper arms on the pad with elbows bent slightly, holding the handle. 3. Curl the cable upward by bending your elbows, bringing it toward your shoulders. 4. Lower with control, maintaining contact with the pad throughout to isolate your biceps.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.instructions:
The reverse cable fly, also known as the cable rear delt fly, is a deltoid muscle strengthening and definition exercise. It’s one of the best isolation exercises for your back and posterior deltoid.This workout targets your posterior (back) deltoids while using a range of upper body muscles.
Adjust the weight and the pulleys to the right height. You should be able to see the pulleys because they should be above your head.
With your right hand, grab the left pulley, and with your left hand, grab the right pulley, crossing them in front of you. This is where you’ll begin your journey.
Start the movement by moving your arms back and forth while keeping your arms straight.
Pause at the finish of the move for a brief moment before returning the handles to their starting positions.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach an ankle strap to a high cable pulley and lie on your back underneath, holding the attachment with both feet. 2. Bend your knees and bring them toward your chest in a crunching motion, engaging your lower abs. 3. Lower your legs back to the starting position under control. Keep your hands behind your head for support.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from a cable machine with a rope attachment positioned overhead, elbows bent and hands near your head. 2. Extend your arms upward and slightly forward, straightening your elbows fully while keeping them close together. 3. Lower the rope back behind your head in a controlled motion, maintaining tension on your triceps. Feel the stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with a rope attachment at face height, holding each end with elbows bent. 2. Pull the rope toward your face by driving your elbows back and out to the sides, engaging your rear delts. 3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak, then return the rope with control. Avoid using your back to generate momentum.

exercises.name: Cable Russian Twists
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on the floor in front of a cable machine, knees bent and torso leaning back at 45 degrees, holding a handle at chest height. 2. Rotate your torso to one side, extending the cable handle away from your body, feeling your obliques work. 3. Rotate back through center and continue to the other side in a smooth, controlled motion. Keep your chest up throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Seated Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright on a bench in front of a cable machine with a rope attachment at head height, holding the rope behind your head. 2. Crunch forward by flexing your abs and bringing your elbows down toward your thighs. 3. Return to the starting position with control, resisting the cable throughout. Focus on shortening the distance from ribs to hips.

exercises.name: Cable Seated Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright at a cable machine with handles held at your sides, cables attached to low pulleys. 2. Raise the handles out to your sides and slightly upward, keeping a slight bend in your elbows until they reach shoulder height. 3. Lower the handles back to your sides under control. Maintain an upright posture and avoid shrugging your shoulders.

exercises.name: Cable Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from a cable machine with handles at shoulder height, feet staggered for stability. 2. Press the handles upward and slightly forward, extending your arms nearly fully while engaging your shoulders. 3. Lower the handles back to shoulder height under control, maintaining tension on your delts. Avoid arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Cable Shrugs
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with handles at your sides, arms straight, feet hip-width apart. 2. Shrug your shoulders upward toward your ears by raising them as high as possible, squeezing your traps at the top. 3. Lower your shoulders back down under control. Avoid rolling your shoulders backward; use a straight vertical motion.

exercises.name: Cable Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions:
Extend your arm down, then slightly lift your forearm
Extend your wrist in a supinated form (palm up)
Adjust cable height so that the cable handle is in your supinated hand
Perform the movement by
curling your palms and wrists upwards
(optional/variable) Pause at the top
Slowly return to the starting position

exercises.name: Calf Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in the calf raise machine with your knees bent 90 degrees and the balls of your feet on the foot platform. 2. Press the platform down by extending your ankles, raising your heels as high as possible to work your calves. 3. Lower your heels back under control. Move only at the ankle, not the knee.

exercises.name: Calf Press On The Leg Press Machine
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up in a leg press machine and position only the balls of your feet on the bottom of the platform, letting your heels hang off. 2. Point your toes downward and press the platform away, rising onto the balls of your feet to engage your calves. 3. Return by lowering your heels back down toward the floor. Use a controlled tempo and focus on the calf contraction.

exercises.name: Calf Raise On A Dumbbell
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with one foot on a dumbbell, the other foot on the floor, holding a support point with one hand for balance. 2. Rise onto the ball of your working foot, lifting your heel as high as possible to fully engage your calf. 3. Lower your heel back down under control. Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other leg.

exercises.name: Calf Raises - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Step into a resistance band with both feet, shoulder-width apart, and hold the loose ends in your hands at hip height. 2. Rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels high while resisting the band tension. 3. Lower your heels back down in a controlled manner. Maintain an upright torso throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Calf-Machine Shoulder Shrug
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in a calf-shrug machine with your shoulders under the pads, feet flat on the ground or platform. 2. Shrug your shoulders upward as high as possible, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement. 3. Lower your shoulders back to the starting position under control. Perform slow, controlled reps to maximize the contraction.

exercises.name: Car Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself inside or against a car-like object with a low center of gravity, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Hinge at the hips and squat down to grip the object securely with both hands, keeping your back neutral. 3. Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand up, lifting the object to waist height. Lower with control and repeat.

exercises.name: Car Drivers
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell at arm's length at your side, standing upright with feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Rotate your body toward the side holding the barbell, twisting your torso and driving the bar diagonally upward across your body. 3. Bring the bar back to the starting position. Repeat on both sides, engaging your shoulders and core with each rotation.

exercises.name: Chain Handle Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing the anchor point of a chain system, holding the end of the chain at shoulder height with elbows bent. 2. Extend your arm forward by straightening your elbow fully, pressing the chain handle away from your body. 3. Lower the chain back to shoulder height under control, maintaining tension throughout. Repeat for all reps on one arm before switching.

exercises.name: Chain Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up with chains looped over a barbell resting on your chest, standing with feet shoulder-width apart and core engaged. 2. Press the barbell upward, extending your arms fully as the chains lift off the ground and build resistance. 3. Lower the barbell back to your chest as the chains pile on the ground, reducing load at the bottom. The motion increases resistance as you press upward.

exercises.name: Chair Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in a squat machine with your back and shoulders supported, feet on the platform about shoulder-width apart. 2. Extend your legs forward by straightening your knees, driving through your thighs and quads. 3. Bend your knees to return, controlling the descent. Keep a soft bend in your knees at the top; don't lock out.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.instructions: The chin-up (also known as a chin or chinup) is a strength training exercise. People frequently do this exercise with the intention of strengthening muscles such as the latissimus dorsi and biceps, which extend the shoulder and flex the elbow, respectively. In this maneuver, the palms are faced towards the body. It is a form of pull-up in which the range of motion is established in relation to a person's chin.

exercises.name: Circus Bell
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright holding a circus bell (off-center weight) with one hand, the heavy end hanging down toward the ground. 2. Press the bell overhead by extending your arm upward, resisting the rotational torque of the off-center weight. 3. Lower the bell back to shoulder height under control, maintaining stability through your core. Switch hands and repeat.

exercises.name: Clean
exercises.instructions:
Regular olympic lift clean.
Pull bar from ground, catch on shoulders performing a front squat.

exercises.name: Clean and Jerk
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell over your mid-foot, and perform a explosive pull, rising onto your toes. 2. Drop under the bar in a quarter squat, catching it on your shoulders with elbows high, then drive back to standing. 3. Dip your knees slightly, then explosively extend to press the barbell overhead, moving your head back slightly. 4. Catch the bar at arm's length and stabilize before lowering.

exercises.name: Clean and Press
exercises.instructions:
The First Pull: Lift the bar from the floor to knee-height by driving with the legs, keeping the angle of your back constant.
The "Power" Position: As the bar reaches mid-thigh, explosively shrug and extend your hips to create vertical momentum.
The Quick Elbow Turnover: In the catch phase, rotate your elbows rapidly under the bar to create a "shelf" on your front deltoids.
The Vertical Press: Press the bar in a straight line; your head should shift slightly forward once the bar clears your forehead to reach full lockout.

exercises.name: Clean Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Position a barbell over your mid-foot with feet hip-width apart, hands shoulder-width apart just outside your legs. 2. Drive through your heels and explosively extend your knees and hips, pulling the barbell upward close to your body. 3. Rise onto your toes at the peak, using your hamstrings and glutes to generate power. Lower the barbell back down under control.

exercises.name: Clean from Blocks
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell at mid-shin on blocks. 2. Grip the bar with elbows high and slightly forward. 3. Explosively extend hips and knees, shrugging the barbell upward. 4. Catch the bar on your shoulders as you dip into a quarter squat. 5. Keep your chest tall and core braced throughout.

exercises.name: Clean Pull
exercises.instructions: 1. Position feet hip-width apart with barbell at mid-shin, hands slightly outside shoulders. 2. Drive through your heels, explosively extending hips and knees while pulling the bar straight up. 3. Shrug at the top, maintaining a neutral spine. 4. Lower the bar under control to the starting position. Stay aggressive through the pull without catching.

exercises.name: Clean Shrug
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell in front of you at hip height. 2. Drive your heels into the ground and shrug your shoulders powerfully upward. 3. Rise onto your toes at the peak, maintaining a neutral spine. 4. Lower the bar with control. Keep movements explosive and avoid excessive arm bend.

exercises.name: Clock Push-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Start in a push-up position. 2. Perform a push-up, then walk one hand to 1 o'clock position, repeat. 3. Continue moving clockwise around your body until you complete the circle. 4. Maintain a rigid plank position throughout. Move deliberately to strengthen stabilizers.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench, hands positioned 6-8 inches apart on the barbell. 2. Lower the bar to your mid-chest with control, elbows tucked closer to your body. 3. Press the bar explosively upward, engaging your triceps intensely. 4. Keep your shoulders packed and core tight. Avoid flaring elbows excessively.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at shoulder height, hands close together and palms facing forward. 2. Press the dumbbells upward and slightly inward in an arc. 3. Lower with control back to shoulder height, maintaining close grip throughout. 4. Keep your wrists neutral and chest engaged. Squeeze triceps at lockout.

exercises.name: Close-Grip EZ Bar Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding an EZ bar with hands 6 inches apart on the inner handles. 2. Keep elbows stationary at your sides and curl the bar toward your chin. 3. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower with control. 4. Maintain an upright torso and avoid swinging the weight. Focus on the biceps contraction.

exercises.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl with Band
exercises.instructions: 1. Step on a resistance band and hold an EZ bar with hands close together, band looped under the bar. 2. Curl the bar upward against band tension, keeping elbows fixed. 3. Squeeze the biceps peak and lower under control. 4. The band adds increasing resistance as you curl. Maintain strict form throughout.

exercises.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar with hands 8 inches apart, bar at chest height. 2. Press upward, extending your triceps, with a slight angle inward. 3. Lower back to chest, keeping elbows tucked. 4. Keep your back flat and core engaged. This emphasizes the triceps over chest.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a cable pulldown station with a close-grip handle, knees tucked under the pad. 2. Pull the handle down toward your sternum, leading with your elbows. 3. Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then return with control to the start. 4. Keep your chest proud and avoid leaning back too much. Focus on lat engagement.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up off of a Dumbbell
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself in a push-up stance with hands on a dumbbell, hands close together. 2. Lower your body toward the dumbbell, keeping elbows tucked to your sides. 3. Press back up to the top, engaging your triceps heavily. 4. Maintain a rigid plank and neutral spine. This position intensifies triceps activation.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Standing Barbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with hands 6-8 inches apart. 2. Curl the bar toward your chest, keeping elbows glued to your sides. 3. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower under control. 4. Avoid momentum and arching your back. Keep tension constant on the biceps.

exercises.name: Cocoons
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with arms and legs extended. 2. In one explosive motion, tuck your knees to your chest while bringing your arms around your legs. 3. Extend back to the starting position. 4. Move dynamically and maintain control. This targets your core through spinal flexion and hip flexion.

exercises.name: Conan's Wheel
exercises.instructions: 1. Straddle a wheel apparatus or ab wheel, gripping handles with both hands. 2. Roll forward, extending your body as far as possible while maintaining spinal alignment. 3. Drive through your quads and core to roll back to the start. 4. Keep your core extremely braced and abs tight. Scale intensity by reducing range of motion.

exercises.name: Concentration Curls
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench with feet flat, a dumbbell in one hand resting between your thighs. 2. Curl the dumbbell upward, focusing on squeezing the biceps at the peak. 3. Lower slowly under control, fully extending your arm. 4. Keep your elbow stationary against your inner thigh. Eliminate all swinging for pure biceps work.

exercises.name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). 2. Curl one dumbbell diagonally across your body toward the opposite shoulder. 3. Lower with control and repeat on the other side, alternating. 4. Keep elbows relatively stationary. This angle targets the brachialis and outer biceps.

exercises.name: Cross Over - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in the center of band resistance, one end in each hand at shoulder height. 2. Pull the bands diagonally across your body in a hugging motion, bringing hands together at chest level. 3. Pause and squeeze your chest, then return with control to the start. 4. Maintain an upright posture and slight knee bend. Feel the pecs contract throughout.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. 2. Bring your right elbow toward your left knee, crunching upward and rotating your torso. 3. Lower back down and repeat on the other side, alternating. 4. Move with control and focus on the obliques. Keep your neck neutral and core engaged.

exercises.name: Crucifix
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a fixed position on a bar or apparatus with your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height. 2. Keep your legs straight and body in one rigid line for the duration. 3. Breathe steadily and maintain shoulder tension throughout the hold. 4. This is an isometric exercise for shoulder stability. Start with short holds and progress gradually.

exercises.name: Crunch - Hands Overhead
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and hands positioned behind your head or across your chest. 2. Crunch upward, bringing your shoulders off the floor and driving your elbows toward your hips. 3. Squeeze your abs at the top, then lower with control. 4. Keep tension in the abs and avoid pulling on your neck. Move deliberately and avoid momentum.

exercises.name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with your calves and heels resting on a stability ball, arms crossed on your chest or hands behind your head. 2. Crunch upward, driving your shoulders off the floor toward your hips. 3. Lower back down with control. 4. The ball adds instability and engages stabilizers. Keep your hips stable and avoid swinging.

exercises.name: Crunches
exercises.instructions: Lay down on your back a soft surface, the feet are on the floor. Ask a partner or use some other help (barbell, etc.) to keep them fixed, your hands are behind your head. From this position move your upper body up till your head or elbows touch your knees. Do this movement by rolling up your back.

exercises.name: Cuban Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows bent and knuckles facing forward. 2. Externally rotate your shoulders so your elbows point back while keeping the dumbbells at shoulder level. 3. Press the dumbbells overhead in a smooth motion. 4. Lower back through the same path. This combines rotation and pressing for shoulder mobility and strength.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with arms extended upward toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90 degrees. 2. Slowly lower your right arm overhead while straightening your left leg, hovering both inches above the floor. 3. Return to the start and repeat on the opposite side. 4. Keep your lower back flat and core braced throughout. Move with control and precision.

exercises.name: Deadlift with Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell at mid-shin, with bands looped under the bar and around your feet. 2. Drive through your heels, extending hips and knees simultaneously, lifting the bar. 3. Lock out at the hips and knees at the top, then lower with control back to start. 4. Bands add ascending tension. Keep your spine neutral and chest proud throughout.

exercises.name: Deadlift with Chains
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell at mid-shin with chains draped over the bar. 2. Drive through your heels and powerfully extend your hips and knees, pulling the bar. 3. Lock out your hips at the top, then lower the bar under control. 4. Chains add weight as you lift higher. Maintain a neutral spine and explosive drive.

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions: Lay down on a decline bench, the bar should be directly above your eyes, the knees are somewhat angled and the feet are firmly on the floor. Concentrate, breath deeply and grab the bar more than shoulder wide. Bring it slowly down till it briefly touches your chest at the height of your nipples. Push the bar up.

exercises.name: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench with hands close together on the barbell at chest height. 2. Press the bar upward to lockout. 3. Lower the bar behind your head in a skull crusher motion, elbows bent and stationary. 4. Extend back to chest and repeat. This combines pressing and extension for triceps.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench with feet secured, hands behind your head or crossed on chest. 2. Crunch upward, driving your shoulders toward your hips. 3. Squeeze your abs at the top, then lower with control. 4. The decline angle intensifies resistance. Keep tension constant and avoid jerky movements.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions: Take two dumbbells and sit on a decline bench, the feet are firmly on the floor, the head is resting the bench. Hold the weights next to the chest, at the height of your nipples and press them up till the arms are stretched. Let the weight slowly and controlled down.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Flyes
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench holding dumbbells above your chest with a slight elbow bend. 2. Lower the dumbbells in an arc out to the sides, allowing your chest to stretch. 3. Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest, squeezing your pecs. 4. Maintain a slight elbow bend throughout. Focus on the chest stretch and contraction.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench holding one dumbbell in both hands above your chest with arms extended. 2. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending at the elbows, keeping upper arms stationary. 3. Extend your triceps to return to the top. 4. The decline angle intensifies the stretch. Keep movement controlled and feel the triceps work.

exercises.name: Decline EZ Bar Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench holding an EZ bar above your chest with arms extended. 2. Lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping upper arms relatively stationary. 3. Extend your triceps to press the bar back to the start. 4. The EZ bar reduces wrist strain. Control the descent and drive up powerfully.

exercises.name: Decline Oblique Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench with feet secured, hands behind your head or crossed on chest. 2. Crunch upward and rotate, bringing your right elbow toward your left knee. 3. Return and repeat on the opposite side, alternating. 4. The decline adds resistance. Move with control and focus on oblique contraction.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself in a push-up stance with feet elevated on a bench or platform. 2. Lower your body toward the floor, keeping elbows at a 45-degree angle. 3. Press back up to the top, engaging your chest and shoulders. 4. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Elevation increases upper chest activation.

exercises.name: Decline Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a decline bench with hips at the edge and knees bent, hands gripping the bench behind you. 2. Pull your knees toward your chest, lifting your hips upward and rounding your lower spine. 3. Lower back down with control. 4. The decline angle intensifies the movement. Focus on the lower abs pulling the knees up.

exercises.name: Decline Smith Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Set a guided barbell machine's bar to a decline bench and lie back with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. 2. Lower the bar to your lower chest with control. 3. Press the bar back up to lockout, working your lower chest and triceps. Keep your shoulder blades pulled back throughout.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
exercises.instructions:
Preparation
Stand on weight plate, bumper plate, or shallow elevated platform with loaded bar above feet. Squat down and grasp bar with shoulder width or slightly wider overhand or mixed grip.
Execution
Lift bar by extending hips and knees to full extension. Pull shoulders back at top of lift if rounded. Return weights to floor by bending hips back while allowing knees to bend forward, keeping back straight and knees pointed same direction as feet. Repeat.
Comments
Throughout lift, keep hips low, shoulders high, arms and back straight. Knees should point same direction as feet throughout movement. Keep bar close to body to improve mechanical leverage. Grip strength and strength endurance often limit ability to perform multiple reps at heavy resistances. Gym chalk, wrist straps, grip work, and mixed grip can be used to enhance grip. Mixed grip indicates one hand holding with overhand grip and other hand holding with underhand grip. Lever barbell jack can be used to lift barbell from floor for easier loading and unloading of weight plates.
Barbell Deficit Deadlift emphasizes building strength through lowest portion of Deadlift. Target muscle is exercised isometrically. Heavy barbell deadlifts significantly engages Latissmus Dorsi. See Barbell Deficit Deadlift under Gluteus Maximus. Also see Deadlift Analysis.

exercises.name: Dip Machine
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a dip machine with your back against the pad and hands gripping the handles at shoulder height. 2. Press downward, extending your arms and moving the weight stack. 3. Return to the start with control. 4. The machine provides stability. Keep your chest engaged and elbows tracking properly.

exercises.name: Dips - Chest Version
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip parallel bars with hands shoulder-width apart, leaning your torso forward about 30 degrees. 2. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are nearly parallel to the ground. 3. Press back up to the top, engaging your chest and shoulders. 4. Forward lean emphasizes chest. Control the descent and drive through your hands.

exercises.name: Dips - Triceps Version
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip parallel bars with hands shoulder-width apart, keeping your torso upright and legs straight. 2. Lower your body by bending your elbows, with upper arms staying close to your torso. 3. Press back up to lockout, squeezing your triceps at the top. 4. Upright posture targets triceps. Add weight with a belt if needed. Drive up explosively.

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raises
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend forward at the hips so your torso is parallel to the ground, resting your forearms on a bench. 2. Keep your knees slightly bent and rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels. 3. Pause at the top, squeezing your calves, then lower with control. 4. This position isolates the calves effectively. Maintain a tight core and feel the calf contraction.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding two kettlebells at hip level with a slight knee bend, feet hip-width apart. 2. Explosively extend your hips and knees, shrugging one kettlebell upward. 3. Catch it at shoulder height as you dip into a slight squat, then repeat on the opposite side. 4. Alternate continuously in a rhythmic pattern. Keep your core braced throughout.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with two kettlebells at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. 2. Dip your knees, then explosively drive upward and extend your arms overhead. 3. Catch the kettlebells overhead, punching under them as you receive them. 4. Dip your knees to absorb impact and lower back to shoulders. This is a powerful full-body movement.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Push Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with two kettlebells at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart. 2. Dip your knees and explosively extend, using leg drive to accelerate the kettlebells overhead. 3. Receive them overhead and bring them back to shoulders. 4. The leg drive is crucial for power generation. Keep your core tight and shoulders packed.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with two kettlebells on the ground between your feet, feet hip-width apart. 2. Explosively hinge at the hips and knees, then drive upward and pull the kettlebells high. 3. Catch them at shoulder height as you dip under slightly, then stabilize overhead or lower back to shoulders. 4. This demands power and coordination. Keep the kettlebells close to your body.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding two kettlebells overhead at lockout, arms extended, feet hip-width apart. 2. Rotate your torso and carefully lower one hand down toward the floor while keeping one arm overhead. 3. Return to the top position and repeat on the other side. 4. This requires shoulder stability and core strength. Move slowly and maintain perfect control.

exercises.name: Downward Facing Balance
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself face down on all fours with hands directly under shoulders and knees under hips. 2. Extend one leg straight back and slightly up, squeezing your glute as you hold the position. 3. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. 4. Maintain hip alignment and avoid rotating. This targets glute activation and stability.

exercises.name: Drag Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at hip level with hands shoulder-width apart. 2. Curl the bar upward, keeping your elbows and the bar path close to your body throughout the movement. 3. Lower with control, maintaining the same path close to your torso. 4. No elbow extension occurs. This emphasizes the biceps peak contraction without shoulder involvement.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Alternate Bicep Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Curl one dumbbell toward your shoulder while keeping the other arm stationary. 3. Lower and repeat with the opposite arm. 4. Keep elbows stationary and move with control. Alternate in a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows bent at about 90 degrees, feet flat on floor. 2. Press the dumbbells upward and slightly inward in an arc. 3. Lower back to shoulder height with control. 4. Allow a natural range of motion with some chest stretch at the bottom. Drive up explosively.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press with Neutral Grip
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing each other. 2. Press the dumbbells straight up, maintaining the neutral grip throughout. 3. Lower back to shoulder height with control. 4. This grip emphasizes the chest and triceps equally. Keep your wrists neutral and core tight.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing forward. 2. Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, maintaining elbow position and moving through a full range. 3. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower with control. 4. Keep your torso upright and avoid swinging. Focus on the biceps contraction.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand over a dumbbell with feet hip-width apart, hinged at the hips with the dumbbell at floor level. 2. Explosively drive through your heels, extending hips and knees while pulling the dumbbell. 3. Catch the dumbbell at shoulder height as you dip into a quarter squat. 4. Keep your chest proud and core engaged. Drive explosively from the floor.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.instructions: Grab your dumbbells and lay flat on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the ground (use a bench if you have one). Press the weights up, locking out your elbows (A). Lower them slowly until your upper arms are resting on the floor (B) close to your body. Pause here before explosively pressing back up. Squeeze your chest hard and repeat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Flyes
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows. 2. Lower the dumbbells in an arc out to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest. 3. Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest, squeezing your pecs. 4. Maintain elbow bend throughout. Focus on the chest stretch and contraction, not arm strength.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Row
exercises.instructions:
Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Take a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, beginning with the arms straight. This will be your starting position.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Pause at the top of the motion, and then return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on an incline bench set to 45 degrees, holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing down. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until arms are parallel to the ground. 3. Lower with control back to the starting position. 4. The incline angle isolates the shoulders. Keep a slight elbow bend and avoid swinging.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lunges
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet together. 2. Step forward with one leg and lower your body until both knees are bent at 90 degrees. 3. Push back to the starting position and repeat on the opposite leg, alternating. 4. Keep your torso upright and front knee tracking over your toes. Step far enough to maintain balance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your side on a bench or floor, holding a dumbbell in the upper hand above your chest. 2. Raise the dumbbell out to the side in an arc, squeezing your rear delt. 3. Lower with control. 4. The lying position isolates the rear deltoid. Keep your core engaged and avoid rotating your torso.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with elbows bent and forearms up, palms facing each other. 2. Rotate your forearms outward, turning palms down without moving your elbows. 3. Rotate back to the starting position. 4. This isolates the forearm pronators. Control the movement and maintain elbow position.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie face down on an incline bench (or flat bench), holding dumbbells at your sides with a slight arm bend. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the ground. 3. Lower with control back to the start. 4. The prone position isolates rear delts effectively. Feel the rear shoulder squeeze throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with elbows bent and forearms up, palms down. 2. Rotate your forearms upward, turning your palms toward you. 3. Rotate back to palms-down position with control. 4. This isolates forearm supinators. Keep elbows stationary and move through your full range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell at shoulder height in one hand, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Press the dumbbell overhead, extending your arm fully. 3. Lower back to shoulder height with control. 4. Your core stabilizes the unilateral load. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand or sit holding a dumbbell overhead in one hand with your arm extended, elbow slightly bent. 2. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm relatively stationary. 3. Extend your triceps to press the dumbbell back to the top. 4. Keep your core braced. Feel the triceps stretch and contraction throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a single dumbbell at waist height in front of your body with feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Pull the dumbbell upward, leading with your elbow, raising it to shoulder height. 3. Lower with control back to waist level. 4. Your core stabilizes the one-sided load. Complete all reps on one side before switching.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Set an incline bench to 45-60 degrees and lie face-down holding dumbbells with neutral grip. 2. Hang your arms down beneath your shoulders. 3. Curl the dumbbells toward your chest by bending your elbows, keeping them stationary. 4. Lower with control. Keep your core engaged and avoid using momentum.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to shoulder height, leading with your elbows. 3. Pause at the top, then lower back down with control. 4. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and maintain an upright posture.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
exercises.instructions: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in each hand and stepping back into a lunge position, then returning to standing. It primarily targets the glutes, hamstrings, and quadriceps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Scaption
exercises.instructions:
Starting position:
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep a slight bend in your elbows, shoulders relaxed and shoulder blades pulled back.
Execution:
Slowly raise the dumbbells forward and slightly to the side, at about a 30–45° angle from your body (between a front raise and a lateral raise).
Lift until your arms are about shoulder height (do not go overhead).
Pause for a second at the top and feel the activation in your shoulders and scapular stabilizers.
Lower the dumbbells back down under control to the starting position.
Breathing:
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells.
Exhale as you lift them.
Common mistakes:
Using dumbbells that are too heavy (causing jerky movements).
Lifting above shoulder height (puts unnecessary stress on the shoulder joint).
Arching the lower back instead of keeping the movement controlled at the shoulders.
Purpose of the exercise:
Activates the lower trapezius, serratus anterior, and scapular stabilizers.
Helps correct posture and improve shoulder balance.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Seated One-Leg Calf Raise
