exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a preacher curl bench holding dumbbells in a neutral (hammer) grip, arms extended. 2. Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders. 3. Lower them back with control. Keep your upper arms on the pad throughout.

exercises.name: Press Sit-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back holding a barbell at chest level, knees bent, feet flat. 2. Perform a sit-up while pressing the barbell overhead at the top. 3. Lower the barbell and return to the starting position. This combines core flexion with shoulder pressing.

exercises.name: Prone Manual Hamstring
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie face-down on a bench with your legs extended off the edge. 2. Have a partner resist as you curl your heels toward your glutes. 3. Return to the starting position under your partner's resistance. Focus on hamstring contraction.

exercises.name: Prowler Sprint
exercises.instructions: 1. Load a prowler sled and assume a forward-facing position, hands on the handles. 2. Sprint forward at high intensity over a set distance, maintaining steady pace. 3. Walk back for recovery. This builds explosive lower body power and conditioning.

exercises.name: Pull Through
exercises.instructions: 1. Face away from a cable machine with the rope attachment at hip height between your legs. 2. Hinge at the hips and pull the rope toward you by driving your hips forward. 3. Return to the hinge position under control. Emphasize glute activation.

exercises.name: Pullups
exercises.instructions: Grab the pull up bar with a wide grip, the body is hanging freely. Keep your chest out and pull yourself up till your chin reaches the bar or it touches your neck, if you want to pull behind you. Go with a slow and controlled movement down, always keeping the chest out.

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.instructions: Clean your dumbbells onto your shoulders, palms facing in. Take a breath and brace your core. (picture 1)Dip at the knees and use your legs to help (picture 2) press your dumbbells overhead. Lower under control with a slow tempo to your shoulders and repeat.

exercises.name: Push Press - Behind the Neck
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell on your shoulders behind your neck, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Dip your knees slightly, then explosively drive up while pressing the barbell overhead. 3. Lower it back to your shoulders under control. Keep your core braced throughout.

exercises.name: Push Up to Side Plank
exercises.instructions: 1. Start in a push-up position with your body in a straight line. 2. Perform a push-up, then rotate into a side plank at the top, stacking your feet. 3. Return to center and lower to the ground. Hold each position firmly.

exercises.name: Push-Up Wide
exercises.instructions:
​A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to increase the emphasis on the outer chest muscles and shoulders.
​Setup: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Lower: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your core tight.
​Push: Drive through your palms to return to the start position.
​Form: Don't let your lower back sag; keep a straight line from head to heels.

exercises.name: Push-Ups - Close Triceps Position
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself in a push-up stance with hands close together underneath your chest. 2. Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the ground, elbows tight to your ribs. 3. Push back up to the starting position. Keep elbows close for maximum tricep activation.

exercises.name: Push-Ups With Feet Elevated
exercises.instructions: 1. Place your feet on a bench or elevated surface, hands on the ground in push-up position. 2. Lower your chest toward the ground by bending your elbows. 3. Push back up to the starting position. This increases difficulty and upper chest emphasis.

exercises.name: Push-Ups With Feet On An Exercise Ball
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself in a push-up stance with your feet resting on a stability ball. 2. Lower yourself until your chest approaches the ground, maintaining core stability. 3. Push back up against the ball's instability. Keep your core tight to stabilize the ball.

exercises.name: Pushups
exercises.instructions: 1. Assume a push-up position with hands shoulder-width apart, body in a straight line. 2. Lower yourself until your chest nearly touches the ground. 3. Push back up to the starting position. Keep your core engaged and body straight throughout.

exercises.name: Pushups (Close and Wide Hand Positions)
exercises.instructions: 1. Perform push-ups alternating hand positions between close and wide. 2. Lower and press up with each hand variation. 3. Alternate positions for each rep or set. This hits different chest and tricep areas in one exercise.

exercises.name: Rack Delivery
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in front of a power rack with the barbell racked at shoulder height. 2. Unrack the barbell and step back, then press it overhead. 3. Step forward and return it to the rack. This develops shoulder stability and overhead strength.

exercises.name: Rack Pull with Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Set safety pins at knee height; attach resistance bands to the barbell. 2. Pull the barbell from the pins to full hip extension, resisting band tension. 3. Lower it back to the pins under control. Bands increase tension at the top of the lift.

exercises.name: Rack Pulls
exercises.instructions: 1. Set safety pins at mid-shin or knee height; load the barbell. 2. Pull the barbell from the pins to full hip extension. 3. Lower it back to the pins under control. This partial deadlift develops lock-out strength.

exercises.name: Recumbent Bike
exercises.instructions: For this exercise Recumbent Bike is needed. You just sit on it, set level and time and start the workout

exercises.name: Reverse Band Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench with bands looped around the barbell, anchored below to decrease resistance at the top. 2. Lower the bar to your chest, feeling the band tension ease as you descend. 3. Press upward powerfully, fighting harder against band tension at the top. 4. Keep elbows tucked and spine neutral for tricep engagement.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Box Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell on your shoulders with bands anchored above, resisting descent. 2. Descend to touch the box, letting bands assist as you lower. 3. Drive through your heels to stand, accelerating against increasing band tension. 4. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes throughout.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell loaded with bands looped underneath for decreasing assistance at the top. 2. Hinge at the hips and bend knees slightly to grip the bar, back straight. 3. Drive through your heels to stand, pulling the bar close to your body. 4. Band assistance helps most at lockout; drive hard from the floor where it's heaviest.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Power Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell on shoulders with bands anchored above. 2. Rapidly descend with control to below parallel, using explosive energy. 3. Drive explosively upward, legs accelerating against increasing band resistance. 4. Maintain an upright torso and controlled depth for quad and glute development.

exercises.name: Reverse Band Sumo Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes angled out, barbell loaded with bands for decreasing resistance. 2. Hinge slightly and grip the bar, keeping your chest up and weight in your heels. 3. Drive through your entire foot, extending hips and knees to stand tall. 4. Bands assist most at the top; focus power from the ground up.

exercises.name: Reverse Barbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell with an overhand (pronated) grip, arms extended at your sides. 2. Bend your elbows to curl the bar upward, keeping your upper arms stationary. 3. Lower the bar with control back to the starting position. 4. This grip targets the forearm extensors; keep wrists stable and elbows at your sides.

exercises.name: Reverse Barbell Preacher Curls
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at the preacher bench with your arms draped over the pad, holding an EZ-bar with an overhand grip. 2. Curl the bar upward toward your face, focusing on bicep tension. 3. Lower slowly back to full extension, stopping just short of locking out. 4. The preacher pad isolates the bicep; keep your back against the pad for control.

exercises.name: Reverse Cable Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with the handle at waist height, using an overhand grip. 2. Curl the cable toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows stationary and at your sides. 3. Return to starting position with controlled resistance. 4. The overhand grip emphasizes forearm development; maintain constant tension on the cable.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions:
Lay down
Place your hands near your butt (often slightly in front or under or both)
Raise your legs, but about 70% of the way you should be able to also raise your pelvis
(optional/variable) Hold 1/2 seconds at the top
Go back to starting position

exercises.name: Reverse Flyes
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms slightly bent, lean forward at the hips. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides in an arc, leading with your elbows. 3. Return to the starting position with control, squeezing your rear deltoids. 4. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and avoid using momentum; this targets the back shoulders.

exercises.name: Reverse Flyes With External Rotation
exercises.instructions: 1. Lean forward holding dumbbells with bent elbows, rotating your wrists so palms face backward. 2. Raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, rotating your arms outward to increase rear delt and rotator cuff engagement. 3. Lower with control, maintaining the external rotation. 4. This variation emphasizes shoulder stability and rear deltoid development.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Bent-Over Rows
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip, bend forward at the hips with knees slightly bent, chest nearly parallel to the floor. 2. Pull the barbell toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back. 3. Lower the bar with control to full extension. 4. The underhand grip shifts emphasis to upper back and biceps; keep your core braced to protect your lower back.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Triceps Pushdown
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with the handle at chest height, using an underhand grip. 2. Push the handle downward, extending your elbows fully at the bottom. 3. Return to the starting position with controlled resistance. 4. Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows at your sides; the underhand grip targets the inner triceps.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
exercises.instructions:
Lie face-down on a bench with your legs hanging off the edge.
Bend your hips so your thighs are vertical, bending your knees at the same time so your shins stay horizontal.
Straighten out your legs so they are not bent and your toes are pointing backwards horizontally.
Return to the original position, and repeat.

exercises.name: Reverse Machine Flyes
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at the reverse fly machine with your chest against the pad, hands on the handles. 2. Pull the handles outward in an arc, focusing on contracting your rear deltoids. 3. Return to the starting position slowly under control. 4. Let your shoulder blades drive the movement; avoid using chest muscles.

exercises.name: Reverse Plate Curls
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a weight plate with an overhand grip, arms at your sides. 2. Curl the plate upward toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows stationary. 3. Lower the plate with control to the starting position. 4. The offset weight distribution challenges your biceps uniquely; maintain wrist position.

exercises.name: Reverse Triceps Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a bench with an underhand grip on a barbell held above your chest. 2. Lower the bar toward your chest, keeping elbows at 45 degrees from your body. 3. Press the bar back to the starting position, extending your triceps. 4. The underhand grip emphasizes the triceps; keep your shoulders stable and core braced.

exercises.name: Rickshaw Carry
exercises.instructions: 1. Load a rickshaw apparatus and grip the handles firmly, standing upright. 2. Walk forward with controlled, deliberate steps, maintaining an upright posture. 3. Complete the prescribed distance or time without putting down the load. 4. Brace your core and avoid leaning; this builds grip strength and stability.

exercises.name: Rickshaw Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Approach the rickshaw apparatus with feet hip-width apart, hands gripping the handles. 2. Keep your chest up and drive through your legs to stand, lifting the machine. 3. Return to the ground under control, hinging slightly at the hips. 4. Your legs drive the lift; maintain an upright posture and neutral spine throughout.

exercises.name: Ring Dips
exercises.instructions: Dips peformed on gymnastic rings.

exercises.name: Rocking Standing Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at chest height or with arms at your sides. 2. Rise onto the balls of your feet, then rock back onto your heels while holding the elevated position. 3. Return to flat feet and repeat, alternating the rocking motion. 4. This variation challenges calf stability; keep your body upright and core engaged.

exercises.name: Rocky Pull-Ups/Pulldowns
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip an overhead bar with hands shoulder-width apart, feet off the ground. 2. Pull your body upward explosively in quick, rhythmic motions. 3. Lower with control and repeat in rapid succession. 4. Speed and explosivity develop lats and back power; maintain strict form despite the tempo.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.instructions: DL from top to pos 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WtWtjViRsKo

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift from Deficit
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand on a platform, feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell at hip height. 2. Hinge at your hips and lower the bar along your legs, keeping your back straight. 3. Feel a deep hamstring stretch at the bottom, then drive your hips forward to stand. 4. The deficit increases range; never round your lower back.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.instructions: 1. Grasp the rope at chest height with both hands, feet on the ground. 2. Climb upward using your hands and legs in coordinated motions, pulling and driving. 3. Descend under control using controlled hand and leg movements. 4. Engage your lats and grip throughout; this demands full-body pulling strength.

exercises.name: Rope Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Face a high cable pulley with the rope attachment, kneel on the floor. 2. Pull the rope downward, flexing your abs and bringing your chest toward your hips. 3. Return to the starting position with control. 4. Keep your hips stationary and focus on abdominal contraction; avoid using arm strength.

exercises.name: Rope Jumping
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the rope handles at hip height with a relaxed grip, elbows bent. 2. Jump rhythmically, turning the rope overhead while staying light on your feet. 3. Maintain a steady pace for the prescribed duration or reps. 4. This builds leg endurance and coordination; keep your jumps low and controlled.

exercises.name: Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with the rope overhead, arms extended. 2. Pull the rope downward in an arc, keeping your arms straight and pulling with your lats. 3. Return to the starting position with control. 4. This isolates the lats without arm involvement; maintain a slight bend in your elbows.

exercises.name: Rowing, Stationary
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on the rowing machine, feet secured on the footplate, hands holding the handle. 2. Drive with your legs first, then hinge back and pull the handle to your chest. 3. Return by extending your arms, hinging forward, and bending your knees. 4. Maintain a steady, powerful rhythm; breathe consistently throughout the duration.

exercises.name: Running, Treadmill
exercises.instructions: 1. Step onto the treadmill with a steady pace, maintaining good posture and arm swing. 2. Run at your target pace for the prescribed distance or time, breathing rhythmically. 3. Gradually slow down to cool down before stepping off. 4. Keep your core engaged and land midfoot; avoid slapping your feet on the belt.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.instructions:
Hold a dumbbell, barbell weight or something else that is heavy with both hands, but make sure it is not too heavy and you are able to keep in form.
Lean back to a 45-degree angle from the floor. For an extra challenge, lift your feet off the floor.
Rotate your arms to one side to the same level as your chest, touch the floor for a little extra challenge, and then do the same to the other side. When you're back in your original position after doing both sides it will count as 1 rep.

exercises.name: Sandbag Load
exercises.instructions: 1. Approach the sandbag with feet shoulder-width apart, bending at your knees. 2. Grip the sandbag and drive through your legs to lift it explosively to a platform or shoulder. 3. Set it down with control and reset for the next rep. 4. Use your legs to drive the movement; keep your back straight and core braced.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Hang from a bar with arms fully extended, feet off the ground. 2. Pull your body up slightly by retracting your shoulder blades, keeping elbows straight. 3. Lower back to full extension. 4. This targets the scapulae and traps; it's a small, controlled movement, not a full pull-up.

exercises.name: Seated Band Hamstring Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright holding a band anchored above, one leg extended with the band looped around your foot. 2. Curl your leg downward against the band resistance, bringing your heel toward your glute. 3. Return to the starting position with control. 4. Keep your torso stable; isolate the hamstring and avoid swinging.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Military Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright on a bench with a barbell held at shoulder height, hands just wider than shoulder-width. 2. Press the bar overhead in a straight line, locking out your elbows. 3. Lower the bar back to shoulder height with control. 4. Keep your core tight and avoid arching your lower back; this builds shoulder and tricep strength.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Twist
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright holding a barbell across your shoulders, feet planted on the floor. 2. Rotate your torso to one side, keeping your hips stationary. 3. Return to center and rotate to the opposite side. 4. This targets the obliques; move deliberately and avoid twisting with momentum.

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit bent forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm bent, elbow near your chest. 2. Extend the dumbbell backward, straightening your arm fully. 3. Lower with control back to the starting position. 4. Keep your elbow stationary and core engaged; this isolates the triceps on one arm.

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit bent forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows. 3. Lower with control back to the starting position. 4. The forward lean targets your rear deltoids; avoid using momentum.

exercises.name: Seated Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit bent forward at the hips, holding dumbbells in each hand with arms bent, elbows near your chest. 2. Extend the dumbbells backward simultaneously, straightening your arms fully. 3. Lower with control back to the starting position. 4. Keep both elbows stationary; this bilateral variation builds tricep strength evenly.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Rows
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at the cable machine with feet planted, torso upright, holding the handle at chest height. 2. Pull the handle toward your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your back. 3. Return to the starting position with controlled resistance. 4. Keep your chest up and avoid leaning back; focus on trap and upper back contraction.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright at a cable machine with the handle at shoulder height. 2. Press the handle overhead in a straight line, extending your arms fully. 3. Return to shoulder height with control. 4. Cable tension at the top makes the lockout hardest; keep your core tight throughout.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on the calf raise machine with your toes on the platform, weight on your knees. 2. Push through your toes to raise your heels as high as possible. 3. Lower your heels below the platform level for a full stretch. 4. Use the full range of motion; this targets the soleus muscle under the main calf.

exercises.name: Seated Close-Grip Concentration Barbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench holding a barbell with a close grip, arms extended toward the floor. 2. Curl the bar upward, focusing on bicep contraction and limiting movement to your forearms. 3. Lower with control to the starting position. 4. The close grip and isolation emphasize the inner biceps; avoid swinging the weight.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides. 2. Curl both dumbbells upward simultaneously toward your shoulders. 3. Lower with control back to full extension. 4. Keep your back against the bench and elbows at your sides; this prevents cheating.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Inner Biceps Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright holding dumbbells with palms facing inward (neutral grip), arms at your sides. 2. Curl the dumbbells upward, rotating your wrists so palms face your shoulders at the top. 3. Lower with control, rotating back to neutral. 4. The rotation targets the inner biceps differently; maintain tension throughout.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a dumbbell in one hand with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing down. 2. Lower the dumbbell by dropping your wrist downward, feeling your forearm working. 3. Curl the dumbbell back up to the starting position. 4. Keep your forearm still and move only at the wrist; this isolates the forearm extensors.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a dumbbell in one hand with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing up. 2. Curl the dumbbell upward by bending your wrist, keeping your forearm stationary. 3. Lower back to the starting position with control. 4. This targets the forearm flexors; keep movement isolated to the wrist joint.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, feet planted. 2. Press the dumbbells overhead in a straight line, extending your arms fully. 3. Lower with control back to shoulder height. 4. Maintain neutral wrists and keep your core engaged; this builds shoulder and tricep power.

exercises.name: Seated Flat Bench Leg Pull-In
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench, hands gripping behind you for support, legs extended in front. 2. Pull your knees toward your chest in a tucking motion, rounding your spine. 3. Extend your legs back to the starting position with control. 4. This is a bodyweight ab exercise; increase difficulty by holding dumbbells.

exercises.name: Seated Good Mornings
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench with a barbell across your shoulders, feet planted firmly. 2. Bend forward at the hips, lowering your torso toward your thighs while keeping your back straight. 3. Return to upright by extending your hips. 4. Maintain a neutral spine and avoid excessive rounding; this targets the lower back.

exercises.name: Seated Head Harness Neck Resistance
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright with a harness fitted around your head, weighted or resistance-attached. 2. Move your head in the desired direction against the resistance, either forward, backward, or to the side. 3. Return to the starting position with control. 4. Work the traps and neck safely with light resistance; never use excessive weight.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at the leg curl machine with your thighs on the pad, feet hooked under the lever. 2. Curl the lever downward by bending your knees, bringing your heels toward your glutes. 3. Extend your legs back to the starting position with control. 4. Keep your upper body still and hips pressed into the pad; focus on hamstring contraction.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Tucks
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on a bench or chair, hands gripping the edge for support, legs extended in front. 2. Pull your knees toward your chest while tilting your torso forward slightly. 3. Extend your legs back to the starting position. 4. This isolates the abs; for difficulty, hold your legs in the up position briefly.

exercises.name: Seated One-arm Cable Pulley Rows
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at the cable machine with one arm extended, gripping the single-arm handle. 2. Pull the handle toward your torso, driving your elbow back and rotating slightly. 3. Return to the starting position with control. 4. One arm at a time allows you to focus on unilateral trap and back development.

exercises.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Down Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a dumbbell in one hand with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm down. 2. Lower the dumbbell by dropping your wrist downward against gravity. 3. Curl back up, isolating the forearm extensors. 4. Keep your forearm stationary and work only at the wrist joint.

exercises.name: Seated One-Arm Dumbbell Palms-Up Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a dumbbell in one hand with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm up. 2. Curl the dumbbell upward using only your wrist. 3. Lower back down with control. 4. This single-arm variation prevents the stronger arm from dominating.

exercises.name: Seated Palm-Up Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a barbell with an underhand grip, your forearms resting on your thighs. 2. Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting it toward your body. 3. Lower back to the starting position with control. 4. This isolates the forearm flexors; keep your forearms flat throughout.

exercises.name: Seated Palms-Down Barbell Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit holding a barbell with an overhand grip, your forearms resting on your thighs. 2. Lower the barbell by dropping your wrists downward, extending at the wrist joint. 3. Curl back up, squeezing your forearm extensors. 4. Minimize forearm movement; isolate the wrist motion.

exercises.name: Seated Side Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet planted. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows. 3. Lower with control back to the starting position. 4. The seated position prevents leg drive; focus on your side delts.

exercises.name: Seated Triceps Press
exercises.instructions: Sit down on a back (better with back support). Take a dumbbell firmly with both hands and hold it with extended arms over your head. With your palms facing upward and holding the weight of the dumbbell, slowly lower the weight behind your head.

exercises.name: Seated Two-Arm Palms-Up Low-Pulley Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit facing the cable machine with your forearms on the bench, hands holding the bar with palms up. 2. Curl the bar upward by flexing your wrists against the cable resistance. 3. Lower back to the starting position with control. 4. Constant cable tension throughout the range isolates the forearm flexors.

exercises.name: See-Saw Press (Alternating Side Press)
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit or stand holding two dumbbells at shoulder height, one in each hand. 2. Press one dumbbell overhead while the other dumbbell stays at shoulder height. 3. Lower the overhead arm and press the opposite side, alternating smoothly. 4. This unilateral variation builds shoulder balance and core stability.

exercises.name: Shotgun Row
exercises.instructions:
Attach a single handle to a low cable.
After selecting the correct weight, stand a couple feet back with a wide-split stance. Your arm should be extended and your shoulder forward. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by retracting the shoulder and flexing the elbow. As you pull, supinate the wrist, turning the palm upward as you go.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with resistance bands anchored under your feet, holding the band handles at shoulder height. 2. Press upward against the band resistance, extending your arms overhead. 3. Lower back to shoulder height with control. 4. Resistance increases at the top where you're strongest; keep your core braced.

exercises.name: Side Bridge
exercises.instructions: Works your obliques and helps stabilize your spine. Lie on your side and support your body between your forearm and knee to your feet.

exercises.name: Side Jackknife
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your side with your body in a straight line, supporting yourself on one forearm and feet. 2. Crunch your torso and hips toward each other, bending at the waist. 3. Return to the starting position and complete your reps on one side before switching. 4. This targets the obliques and side abs; maintain a stable plank position.

exercises.name: Side Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height, leading with your elbows. 3. Lower with control back to your sides. 4. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and avoid excessive leaning; isolate your side deltoids.

exercises.name: Side Laterals to Front Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. 2. Raise the dumbbells out to your sides to shoulder height, then in one fluid motion bring them forward to shoulder height. 3. Reverse the motion back to the starting position. 4. This combination targets multiple shoulder heads; keep movement controlled and deliberate.

exercises.name: Side To Side Chins
exercises.instructions: 1. Grip the pullup bar with hands shoulder-width apart and pull your body up until your chest nears the bar. 2. At the top, shift your chest toward one side, keeping control. 3. Return to center and repeat on the other side, alternating. 4. Lower with controlled descent, engaging your lats throughout.

exercises.name: Single Dumbbell Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a single dumbbell in one hand at your side. 2. Raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is parallel to the ground, isolating the shoulder. 3. Lower it back down with control. Keep your core stable and avoid leaning.

exercises.name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.instructions: A glute bridge, where you use just one leg at a time.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Crossover
exercises.instructions: 1. Set the cable at chest height and grasp the handle with one hand. 2. Stand slightly forward of center and pull the handle across your torso toward your opposite hip, squeezing your chest. 3. Control the resistance back to the start. Maintain an upright posture throughout.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Linear Jammer
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell at shoulder height on one side, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Press the bar forward in a linear motion, extending your arm fully and driving through your shoulder. 3. Return the bar to your shoulder with control. Keep your core braced and spine neutral.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Push-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Assume a push-up position with one hand on the ground and the other behind your back or across your chest. 2. Lower your body, keeping your hips level and core engaged throughout the descent. 3. Press back up, driving through your working arm. Maintain a straight body line.

exercises.name: Single-Leg High Box Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand on a high box on one leg, holding your other leg bent or extended for balance. 2. Lower yourself by bending the standing leg, descending toward the box under control. 3. Drive through your heel to return to standing. Keep your chest up and control the descent.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit on the leg extension machine and set the pad against one leg just above your ankle. 2. Extend your leg straight out, squeezing your quadriceps at the top of the movement. 3. Lower slowly with control back to the start. Do not lock your knee at the top.

exercises.name: Sit-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet firmly on the ground. 2. Engage your core and curl your torso upward, lifting your shoulders off the ground toward your knees. 3. Lower back down with control. Avoid pulling on your neck; drive the movement from your abs.

exercises.name: Skating
exercises.instructions: 1. Move laterally back and forth in a skating motion, driving off one leg at a time. 2. Maintain an athletic stance with your core engaged and arms swinging naturally throughout. 3. Keep a steady cardio pace, focusing on smooth transitions between sides. Sustain your target pace continuously.

exercises.name: Sled Drag - Harness
exercises.instructions: 1. Fasten the harness around your torso securely, ensuring it distributes load evenly. 2. Step forward against the resistance, driving with your quads and glutes as you drag the sled. 3. Maintain a steady forward pace without excessive forward lean. Keep tension in the harness throughout.

exercises.name: Sled Overhead Backward Walk
exercises.instructions: 1. Load the sled and position it on your shoulders, holding it overhead with both hands pressed upward. 2. Walk backward in a controlled manner, maintaining shoulder height and tension in your core throughout. 3. Focus on steady, measured steps. Brace your core to keep the sled stable overhead.

exercises.name: Sled Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the sled or implement at arm's length overhead with your arms extended. 2. Bend your elbows and lower the weight behind your head, feeling a stretch in your triceps. 3. Extend your arms back to the start position with control. Keep your elbows pointing forward throughout.

exercises.name: Sled Push
exercises.instructions:
Load the sled with 25% of your maximum load. If you don’t know this, choose a weight you can push for 10 minutes with short breaks. Beginners may choose to push the sled with no weight.
Stand behind the sled and grab the poles with a high-grip hand position.
Engage your core muscles and start pushing the sled forward as fast as you can, powering through your entire leg. Extend your hips and knees as you move the sled forward. Your foot stance should resemble your natural running position.

exercises.name: Sled Reverse Flye
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself at the sled with hands gripping the handles at chest height. 2. Pull the handles out to the sides in a wide arc, squeezing your rear delts and upper back. 3. Slowly return to the start position with control. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.

exercises.name: Sled Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach yourself to the sled with harness or handles, standing upright. 2. Drive backward explosively, pulling with your traps and upper back, extending your legs fully. 3. Return to the start position with control. Maintain an upright posture and engage your core throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Incline Shoulder Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Set a guided barbell machine's bench to an incline and sit with your back against the pad. 2. Hold the bar with a neutral grip and raise it to shoulder height in a controlled arc, isolating the shoulder. 3. Lower back to the start. Avoid arching your lower back; keep the work in your shoulders.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Behind the Back Shrug
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself under the bar with it resting behind your back on your trapezius. 2. Shrug your shoulders upward, raising the bar slightly without bending your arms. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Keep your chest up and avoid excessive forward lean.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie flat on the bench with your feet on the floor and eyes positioned under the bar. 2. Press the bar upward until your arms are extended but not locked at the elbows. 3. Lower under control to chest level. Keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend at the hips until your torso is parallel to the ground, arms extended below you. 2. Pull the bar toward your lower chest, leading with your elbows and retracting your scapula. 3. Lower with control. Keep your back flat and core braced throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand under the bar with it resting on your traps, positioning the balls of your feet on the platform. 2. Drive through your toes and rise up as high as possible on your calves, feeling the contraction. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Maintain an upright posture throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.instructions: Perform a standard bench press on the smith machine, but have your hands on the bar about shoulder width apart, and keep your elbows close to your body.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Decline Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Set the bench to a decline angle and lie with your head lower than your feet. 2. Press the bar upward from chest level until your arms are extended but not locked. 3. Lower back to your chest with control. Keep your shoulder blades pinned back throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hang Power Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the bar at shoulder height with elbows high, feet hip-width apart. 2. Dip your knees slightly, then explosively drive through your legs to pull the bar upward. 3. Drop under the bar and catch it across your shoulders in a quarter squat, then stand up. Move explosively and land with control.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself with your back on the bench, feet on the floor, and bar across your hips. 2. Drive through your heels and raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. 3. Lower back down with control. Squeeze your glutes at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Set the bench to an incline, lie with your chest forward and eyes positioned under the bar. 2. Press the bar upward until your arms extend, emphasizing your upper chest throughout the movement. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Leg Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in the machine with your feet on the platform at shoulder-width apart, back against the pad. 2. Press your feet away by extending your legs, stopping before your knees lock out completely. 3. Lower the platform back toward your chest with control. Maintain tension in your quads throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine One-Arm Upright Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing the machine with the bar at thigh level, grasping it with one hand only. 2. Pull the bar upward toward your shoulder, leading with your elbow and keeping it high. 3. Lower with control to the start position. Maintain an upright posture and keep the bar close to your body.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Overhead Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing forward with the bar at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Press the bar directly overhead until your arms are extended but elbows not locked. 3. Lower back to shoulder height with control. Keep your core braced and avoid excessive lower back arch.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Pistol Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing forward on one leg, holding the bar at shoulder height for support and balance. 2. Lower yourself into a single-leg squat, descending as deep as you can while maintaining balance and control. 3. Drive through your working leg to return to standing. Control the descent carefully throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Reverse Calf Raises
exercises.instructions: 1. Position the balls of your feet on an elevated surface, heels off the edge, with the bar across your shoulders. 2. Raise your heels as high as possible by contracting your tibialis anterior, feeling the burn in your shins. 3. Lower your heels back down with control. Maintain balance and an upright posture.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.instructions:
Technique and Execution
The Smith machine squat is a variation of the traditional barbell squat that uses a guided, fixed-path barbell. Here's a detailed breakdown of the proper technique:
Starting Position
Foot Placement: Position feet slightly forward of the bar, about shoulder-width apart
Bar Position: Rest the bar on your upper trapezius/shoulders, similar to a traditional back squat
Stance: Feet can be slightly angled outward for natural hip rotation
Squat Movement
Unrack the bar by rotating it to release from the safety hooks
Slowly lower your body by bending knees and hips
Descend until thighs are parallel to the ground (or slightly below)
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement
Drive through your heels to return to the starting position
Benefits and Considerations
Advantages
Reduced Balance Requirements: Fixed bar path makes it easier for beginners
Controlled Movement: Less risk of improper form compared to free weight squats
Isolation: Allows focused leg muscle development

exercises.name: Smith Machine Stiff-Legged Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with slight knee bend, holding the bar in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width grip. 2. Hinge at your hips and lower the bar along your shins as far as you can while maintaining a neutral spine. 3. Drive through your heels to return to standing. Keep your back straight throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Upright Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing forward with the bar at thigh level in front of you. 2. Pull the bar upward toward your neck, driving your elbows high and out to the sides. 3. Lower with control to the start position. Keep your chest up and shoulders back throughout.

exercises.name: Smith Single-Leg Split Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in a split stance with the bar across your shoulders, one leg forward and one back. 2. Lower your back knee toward the ground until your front thigh is nearly parallel to the floor. 3. Press through your front heel to return to standing. Keep your torso upright and front knee tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: Snatch
exercises.instructions: Stand with your feet at hip width and your shins against the bar. Grasp the bar at double shoulder width and, keeping your lower back flat, drive your heels into the floor to begin lifting the bar. When it's above your knees, explosively extend your hips and shrug your shoulders. Let the momentum carry the weight overhead.

exercises.name: Snatch Balance
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell overhead with your arms extended, feet hip-width apart. 2. Dip your knees slightly, then explosively drive upward while pressing the bar overhead. 3. Drop under the bar into a squat to catch it, then stand up to full height. Move explosively and catch the bar with control.

exercises.name: Snatch Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Position your feet hip-width apart with a wide grip on the barbell just inside your legs. 2. Pull the bar upward using your legs and hips, stopping at mid-thigh as if pausing in a snatch pull. 3. Lower the bar back to the floor with control. Maintain a neutral spine throughout the entire movement.

exercises.name: Snatch from Blocks
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up with the bar at mid-shin height on blocks, feet hip-width apart. 2. Pull explosively through your legs, hips, and shoulders, landing in a squat with the bar overhead. 3. Stand up with the weight in a controlled, steady manner. Move explosively and land with balance and stability.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull
exercises.instructions: 1. Set up with a wide grip on the barbell at shin level, feet hip-width apart and shoulders over the bar. 2. Pull explosively through your legs and hips, drawing your elbows high and out to the sides. 3. Return the bar to the floor with control, resetting your position. Maintain a neutral spine throughout.

exercises.name: Snatch Shrug
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell at arm's length in front of you with feet shoulder-width apart and shoulders over the bar. 2. Shrug your shoulders upward explosively, rising up on your toes and pulling the bar toward your body. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Engage your traps fully and finish the movement completely.

exercises.name: Speed Band Overhead Triceps
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a resistance band attached overhead, gripping it with both hands behind your head and arms bent. 2. Extend your arms upward against the band resistance, fully straightening your triceps and extending overhead. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Maintain an upright posture; keep your elbows stationary throughout.

exercises.name: Speed Box Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself over a box with the barbell on your shoulders, feet hip-width apart. 2. Squat down explosively and tap the box lightly, then immediately drive upward as fast as possible. 3. Stand at the top with control. Focus on explosive acceleration off the box with each rep.

exercises.name: Speed Squats
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell across your shoulders and assume a squat stance, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Descend into a squat as quickly as possible, moving through the bottom position smoothly. 3. Drive upward explosively and return to standing. Prioritize speed and explosiveness throughout each rep.

exercises.name: Spell Caster
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a dumbbell vertically in both hands at chest height, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Rotate and reach diagonally toward one side, extending the dumbbell upward and across your body. 3. Return to center and repeat on the other side, alternating sides. Keep your core engaged and rotate from your torso.

exercises.name: Spider Crawl
exercises.instructions: 1. Start in a plank position with your hands under your shoulders and core braced tightly. 2. Crawl forward by bringing one knee toward the same side elbow, then the opposite knee, alternating. 3. Maintain a rigid plank position throughout; avoid rotating your hips. Move in a controlled crawling pattern.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.instructions:
To get the most out of DB Spider Curls, you need an
adjustable weight bench set at a 45-degree incline. This inclined position
allows your arms to hang freely, putting them in an extended start position
with elbows slightly in front of your torso, which is the key to maintaining
low-level isometric tension throughout the movement pattern.
Lie face-down on an adjustable
weight bench with your chest fully supported, holding a pair of dumbbells.
Keep a neutral head position
and don’t crane your neck.
Let your arms hang straight
down with your palms facing forward (for a standard Spider Curl) or palms
facing inward for a Hammer Curl exercise variation.
Keep a stable foot position on
the floor to maintain balance and control.
Start the curl motion by
flexing your biceps muscles and lifting the pair of dumbbells or curl bar
toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbow flexion
controlled. Your arms should stay locked in position with no unnecessary
movement.
Squeeze hard at the top for 1-2 seconds. This
is where maximum tension hits the biceps muscle fibers.
Lower the weight under control
for 3-4 seconds to keep muscles under tension for the entire range of
motion.

exercises.name: Split Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Position the barbell at shin level with a shoulder-width grip, shoulders over the bar. 2. Pull explosively, driving through your legs and landing in a split position with the bar across your shoulders. 3. Step back to a neutral stance with the weight. Keep your core braced and move under the bar with speed.

exercises.name: Split Jerk
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart and core braced. 2. Dip your knees, then drive explosively upward while pressing the bar overhead with force. 3. Step one foot forward and one back to land in a split squat position, catching the bar overhead, then stand up. Move explosively.

exercises.name: Split Snatch
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself at the bar with a wide snatch grip, feet hip-width apart and ready. 2. Pull explosively and land in a split squat position with the bar overhead, catching with control. 3. Stand up with the weight in a controlled manner. Move explosively and land with balance and stability.

exercises.name: Split Squat with Dumbbells
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, step forward into a lunge position with one leg. 2. Lower your back knee toward the ground, sinking into the lunge with control and staying upright. 3. Push through your front heel to return to standing. Maintain an upright torso and controlled descent.

exercises.name: Squat Jerk
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart and ready to move. 2. Dip your knees, then drive upward and press the bar overhead as you squat down under it. 3. Catch the bar overhead in a squat position, then stand up with control. Move explosively and land with balance.

exercises.name: Squat with Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself under the barbell with bands looped under your feet and attached at the top, adding resistance. 2. Squat down, controlling the increasing band tension as you descend to the bottom position. 3. Drive upward to standing, pressing against the band resistance throughout. Keep tension steady and controlled.

exercises.name: Squat with Chains
exercises.instructions: 1. Load the barbell with plates and chains, positioning yourself under the bar and setting up your stance. 2. Squat down, feeling the chains' added weight intensify at the bottom of the movement. 3. Drive upward to standing, progressively engaging more chains as you rise. Maintain control and steady form.

exercises.name: Squat with Plate Movers
exercises.instructions: 1. Position yourself on slippery plate movers under the barbell, feet on the smooth surfaces. 2. Squat down, allowing your feet to slide outward as you descend, deepening your squat range. 3. Drive upward and inward with your legs, sliding your feet back together. Maintain control of the sliding motion.

exercises.name: Squats - With Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the band handles and stand on the band, positioning your feet hip-width apart and engaged. 2. Squat down against the band resistance, controlling the increasing tension as you descend. 3. Drive through your heels to return to standing. Keep the band under tension and maintain an upright posture.

exercises.name: Stairmaster
exercises.instructions: 1. Enter the machine and set your preferred intensity level, resistance, and target duration. 2. Maintain a steady climbing pace, stepping deliberately and avoiding excessive forward lean on the handles. 3. Keep your core engaged and find a sustainable rhythm you can sustain for your cardio duration. Avoid leaning.

exercises.name: Standing Alternating Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding dumbbells at shoulder height with elbows bent. 2. Press one dumbbell overhead while keeping the other at your shoulder, extending fully. 3. Lower that arm and press the opposite dumbbell. Alternate sides in a controlled rhythm. Keep your core braced throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright with the barbell resting across your shoulders, feet hip-width apart. 2. Drive through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as possible, squeezing your calves. 3. Lower your heels back to the floor with control. Pause at the top of each rep for maximum contraction.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Press Behind Neck
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the barbell behind your neck at shoulder height. 2. Press the bar straight overhead, extending your arms fully but not locking your elbows. 3. Lower the bar back behind your neck with control. Maintain an upright posture and keep your core engaged.

exercises.name: Standing Bent-Over One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend forward at the hips, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm bent at your side. 2. Extend your tricep, straightening your arm and reaching the dumbbell backward and upward. 3. Lower back to the bent position with control. Keep your elbow stationary throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Standing Bent-Over Two-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Bend forward at the hips, holding dumbbells in both hands with your arms bent at your sides. 2. Extend your triceps, straightening both arms and reaching the dumbbells backward and upward. 3. Lower back to the bent position with control. Keep your elbows stationary; move only at the elbow joint.

exercises.name: Standing Biceps Cable Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing the cable machine with the handle at waist height, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Curl the handle toward your chest, bending your elbows and squeezing your biceps at the top. 3. Lower back to the start with control. Keep your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Standing Bradford Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold the barbell at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart and ready to move. 2. Press the bar forward from your chest, then push it behind your neck, then lower back to your shoulders. 3. Reverse the motion back to start, completing the circular press pattern. Move slowly and control the bar path.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Chest Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Face away from a cable machine set at chest height, holding both handles at your sides. 2. Press the handles forward and across your body, extending your arms and engaging your chest fully. 3. Return to the start position with control. Maintain an upright posture and stable stance throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Lift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with the handle set high, grasping it with both hands at shoulder height. 2. Rotate your torso and pull the handle diagonally downward across your body toward your opposite hip. 3. Return to the start with control. Engage your core and rotate from your torso, not your arms.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand perpendicular to the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handle at chest height. 2. Rotate your torso diagonally downward, pulling the cable from high to low across your body. 3. Return to center with control, resisting the cable's pull. Keep your core braced and spine neutral throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.instructions: Get onto the calf raises machine, you should able to completely push your calves down. Stand straight, don't make a hollow back and don't bend your legs. Pull yourself up as high as you can. Make a small pause of 1 - 2 seconds and go slowly down.

exercises.name: Standing Concentration Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended, place your other hand on your hip. 2. Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, focusing on isolating your biceps without swinging. 3. Lower it back down with control. Avoid momentum—this targets peak biceps contraction.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, feet hip-width apart. 2. Press through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes, squeezing your calves at the top. 3. Lower back down with control. Keep the motion smooth and maintain an upright posture.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold a dumbbell at shoulder height in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart and core braced. 2. Press the dumbbells overhead in a straight line, extending your elbows fully. 3. Lower back to shoulder level under control. Don't lock out your elbows at the top.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Reverse Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing inward. 2. Curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders while maintaining a neutral wrist position. 3. Lower them back to your sides. This variation emphasizes your forearms and outer biceps.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Straight-Arm Front Delt Raise Above Head
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, arm straight, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Raise the dumbbell in front of you in a straight arm motion, lifting it overhead. 3. Lower it back down smoothly. Keep your shoulder packed and core tight—don't use momentum.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell with both hands behind your head, elbows bent and upper arms stationary. 2. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell overhead. 3. Lower it back behind your head under control. Keep your elbows tucked in—don't let them flare.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Upright Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, feet hip-width apart. 2. Raise the dumbbells vertically up toward your chin, keeping them close to your body and leading with your elbows. 3. Lower back down under control. This movement targets your traps and shoulders.

exercises.name: Standing Front Barbell Raise Over Head
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at thigh level with hands shoulder-width apart, feet hip-width apart. 2. Raise the barbell in front of you in a straight-arm motion until it reaches overhead. 3. Lower it back down with control. Avoid hyperextending your lower back—keep your core engaged.

exercises.name: Standing Inner-Biceps Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells with elbows at your sides, palms facing forward. 2. Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping elbows glued to your torso. 3. Lower them back down. This angle maximizes inner biceps peak and contraction.

exercises.name: Standing Leg Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand at the leg curl machine, place your foot under the curl pad with your body upright. 2. Curl your leg upward, bringing your heel toward your glutes, squeeze, then lower. 3. Keep your hips stable and avoid arching your lower back during the curl.

exercises.name: Standing Low-Pulley Deltoid Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand sideways to the cable machine, grasp the handle at waist level in the hand farther from the machine. 2. Raise your arm out to the side in an arc, lifting the weight to shoulder height. 3. Lower it back down smoothly. Keep a slight bend in your elbow throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Low-Pulley One-Arm Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing away from the cable machine, hold the handle overhead with your elbow bent, upper arm stationary. 2. Extend your elbow to straighten your arm fully. 3. Lower the handle back down under control. Keep tension on your triceps—don't rest at the bottom.

exercises.name: Standing Military Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hold a barbell at shoulder height with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. 2. Press the barbell directly overhead, locking out your elbows at the top. 3. Lower it back to shoulder height under control. Brace your core and avoid excessive lower back arch.

exercises.name: Standing Olympic Plate Hand Squeeze
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding an Olympic plate in one hand with fingers and thumb on the smooth sides. 2. Squeeze the plate firmly for the duration, maximizing grip tension. 3. Release and rest. This isometric builds forearm and grip strength intensely.

exercises.name: Standing One-Arm Cable Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand sideways to the cable machine, grasp the handle with the arm closest to the machine, let it hang at your side. 2. Curl the handle toward your shoulder against the cable resistance. 3. Lower it back down under control. This single-arm variation allows greater range and isolation.

exercises.name: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Curl Over Incline Bench
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand behind an incline bench, hold a dumbbell in one hand, let your arm hang over the backrest. 2. Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, keep your arm extended back as the bench anchors your movement. 3. Lower it back down. The bench position removes momentum and intensifies biceps contraction.

exercises.name: Standing One-Arm Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell overhead in one hand, elbow bent and upper arm vertical. 2. Extend your elbow to straighten your arm fully, keep your shoulder stable. 3. Lower it back behind your head. Don't let your elbow drift forward—keep it under your wrist.

exercises.name: Standing Overhead Barbell Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell overhead with both hands, elbows bent, upper arms stationary. 2. Extend your elbows to press the barbell slightly forward and upward, fully lengthening your triceps. 3. Lower it back behind your head. Keep your core braced to prevent lower back arching.

exercises.name: Standing Palm-In One-Arm Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright, hold a dumbbell at shoulder height in one hand with your palm facing inward. 2. Press the dumbbell overhead while rotating your wrist so your palm faces forward at the top. 3. Lower it back to shoulder height. This unilateral variation demands core stability.

exercises.name: Standing Palms-In Dumbbell Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing each other. 2. Press both dumbbells overhead, maintaining the neutral grip position throughout the movement. 3. Lower them back to shoulder level. This angle reduces shoulder strain compared to a traditional press.

exercises.name: Standing Palms-Up Barbell Behind The Back Wrist Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell behind your back with palms facing upward, arms extended. 2. Curl the barbell upward using only your wrist and forearm muscles, lift as high as possible. 3. Lower it back down with control. This isolates the forearm flexors intensely.

exercises.name: Standing Rope Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing the cable machine holding the rope attachment at chest level, knees slightly bent. 2. Crunch downward by contracting your abs and driving your elbows toward your hips. 3. Return to standing with control. Keep your neck neutral—pull with your abs, not your neck.

exercises.name: Standing Towel Triceps Extension
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a towel draped over your shoulders, hands gripping each end behind your back, elbows bent. 2. Extend your elbows to pull the towel downward and back until your arms straighten. 3. Return to bent position. This uses your body weight and towel resistance to target your triceps.

exercises.name: Step Mill
exercises.instructions: 1. Step onto the step mill machine, set your desired pace and resistance level. 2. Maintain a steady rhythm, stepping continuously as the machine moves the pedals. 3. Breathe steadily throughout—maintain a pace you can sustain for your target duration.

exercises.name: Step-up with Knee Raise
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a bench or step, step up onto it with one leg and drive your opposite knee upward explosively. 2. Step back down under control and repeat. 3. Alternate legs. This targets your glutes and quad power while building unilateral strength.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Barbell Good Morning
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, place a barbell across your upper back, keep your legs straight throughout. 2. Hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso until you feel a strong hamstring and lower back stretch. 3. Drive through your heels to return upright. Maintain a neutral spine—don't round your lower back.

exercises.name: Stiff-Legged Barbell Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, grasp a barbell at thigh level, keep your legs nearly straight. 2. Hinge at your hips and lower the barbell toward your shins, feeling the hamstring stretch intensely. 3. Drive your hips forward to stand back up. Keep your chest up and spine neutral throughout.

exercises.name: Stiff-Legged Dumbbell Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, feet hip-width apart, legs nearly straight. 2. Hinge forward at your hips, lowering the dumbbells toward your shins while maintaining a strong hamstring stretch. 3. Push your hips forward to return upright. Minimize knee bend—this isolates the posterior chain.

exercises.name: Straight Bar Bench Mid Rows
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie face-down on a bench set to decline, grasp a straight bar above your chest. 2. Row the bar downward toward your mid-chest, retract your shoulder blades, squeeze your back. 3. Lower it back to the starting position with control. Keep your chest on the bench—avoid momentum.

exercises.name: Straight Raises on Incline Bench
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit upright on an incline bench, hold a barbell at arm's length in front of your chest. 2. Raise the barbell straight up overhead in a controlled motion, keep your arms extended. 3. Lower it back to chest level. The incline position increases shoulder activation.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie perpendicular across a bench with your chest and upper back on it, hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest. 2. Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head, keep your arms nearly straight, feel your chest stretch. 3. Pull the dumbbell back over your body. This targets your chest and engages your lats.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine with feet hip-width apart, grasp the bar at shoulder height with straight arms. 2. Pull the bar downward in an arc toward your thighs, keep your arms extended throughout. 3. Return to shoulder height. Focus on using your lats and avoid bending your elbows.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.instructions:
Begin with a bar loaded on the ground. Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide, near the collars. Bend at the hips to grip the bar. The arms should be directly below the shoulders, inside the legs, and you can use a pronated grip, a mixed grip, or hook grip. Relax the shoulders, which in effect lengthens your arms.
Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart, with your weight on the back half of your feet. Extend through the hips and knees.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift with Bands
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand inside a barbell with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned outward, bands looped around the barbell and secured. 2. Grip the bar and deadlift it upward, driving through your heels until you stand fully upright. 3. Lower the bar back to the starting position under control. The bands add variable resistance at the top.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift with Chains
exercises.instructions: 1. Load a barbell with chains draped over the sides, stand with feet wider than shoulder-width and toes angled out. 2. Lift the barbell by driving through your heels and extending your hips fully. 3. Lower the bar under control. Chains add progressive resistance as you lift higher.

exercises.name: Suspended Fallout
exercises.instructions: 1. Hold suspension straps at chest height, stand upright and brace your core tightly. 2. Lean forward, extending your arms as you move your body in a line, lean as far as you can control. 3. Return to standing by pulling yourself back using your abs and shoulders. Maintain core tension—don't let your hips sag.

exercises.name: Suspended Push-Up
exercises.instructions: 1. Set suspension straps at mid-height, place your hands in the handles, assume a plank position. 2. Lower your chest toward the ground by bending your elbows, keep your body straight. 3. Press back up to the starting position. The straps increase instability and intensify chest activation.

exercises.name: Suspended Reverse Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Set suspension straps low, lie on your back and place your heels in the handles, hips off the ground. 2. Curl your hips upward and pull your knees toward your chest, crunch your abs. 3. Lower back down under control. Keep your core engaged and movement controlled throughout.

exercises.name: Suspended Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Set suspension straps at mid-length, grasp the handles and lean back until your body is nearly parallel to the ground. 2. Pull your chest toward the handles by retracting your shoulder blades, row powerfully. 3. Lower your body back to the starting position. The angle can be adjusted to increase or decrease difficulty.

exercises.name: Suspended Split Squat
exercises.instructions: 1. Set suspension straps at mid-height, place one foot in a handle behind you, step forward with the other leg. 2. Lower your body by bending your front knee until your back knee nearly touches the ground. 3. Press through your front heel to stand back up. This unilateral variation builds single-leg quad strength and stability.

exercises.name: Svend Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding an Olympic plate against your chest with your palms pressed against the smooth side. 2. Press the plate away from your body, extending your arms fully while maintaining the plate level. 3. Return the plate to your chest. This isometric squeeze targets your chest intensely.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row with Handle
exercises.instructions: 1. Straddle a barbell with a t-bar row handle, grasp the handle and bend forward with a neutral spine, chest up. 2. Row the handle upward toward your chest, squeeze your back muscles at the top. 3. Lower it back down under control. Keep your knees slightly bent to protect your lower back.

exercises.name: Tate Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells at chest height with elbows bent, neutral grip position. 2. Press the dumbbells upward by extending your elbows, keep the dumbbells parallel. 3. Lower them back to chest height. This unique angle targets your triceps and inner chest.

exercises.name: Thigh Abductor
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in the abductor machine with your knees on the pads positioned on the inside, thighs together. 2. Push the pads apart by abducting your hips, squeeze your glutes and outer thighs at the furthest point. 3. Return to the starting position slowly. Maintain an upright posture throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Thigh Adductor
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit in the adductor machine with your knees positioned on the outside pads, hips and back against the seat. 2. Squeeze the pads together by adducting your hips, bringing your thighs together and activating your inner quads. 3. Return to the starting position under control. Move smoothly without jerking.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand in front of a tire in a staggered stance, grip the bottom edge with both hands, chest up. 2. Explosively drive through your legs, extend your hips, and flip the tire over your body. 3. Reset and repeat. This full-body compound movement demands power, speed, and coordination.

exercises.name: Trail Running/Walking
exercises.instructions: 1. Begin at a moderate pace on a trail or hill, maintain a steady cadence and upright posture. 2. Keep a consistent breathing pattern as you move, adjust pace based on terrain difficulty. 3. Continue your desired duration—focus on sustained effort over speed.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand inside a trap bar with feet hip-width apart, grasp the handles at your sides. 2. Deadlift the bar upward by driving through your heels and extending your hips and knees fully. 3. Lower the bar back down under control. The trap bar reduces lower back strain compared to a straight barbell.

exercises.name: Tricep Dumbbell Kickback
exercises.instructions:
Start with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing your torso. Keep your back straight with a slight bend in the knees and bend forward at the waist. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor. Make sure to keep your head up. Your upper arms should be close to your torso and parallel to the floor. Your forearms should be pointed towards the floor as you hold the weights. There should be a 90-degree angle formed between your forearm and upper arm. This is your starting position.
Now, while keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and use your triceps to lift the weights until the arm is fully extended. Focus on moving the forearm.
After a brief pause at the top contraction, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Variations: This exercise can be executed also one arm at a time much like the one arm rows are performed.
Also, if you like the one arm variety, you can use a low pulley handle instead of a dumbbell for better peak contraction. In this case, the palms should be facing up (supinated grip) as opposed to the torso (neutral grip).

exercises.name: Triceps Overhead Extension with Rope
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach a rope to a high cable pulley, stand facing away from the machine, hold the rope overhead with elbows bent. 2. Extend your elbows to straighten your arms and pull the rope down and outward. 3. Return to the bent position under control. The rope allows for hand separation at full extension.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.instructions: Triceps pushdown on cable using lat bar.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown - Rope Attachment
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach a rope to a high cable pulley, stand upright facing the machine, grasp the rope with elbows at your sides. 2. Push the rope downward by extending your elbows, separate the rope ends at the bottom. 3. Return to bent position. The rope provides a full range and hand separation at the end point.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown - V-Bar Attachment
exercises.instructions: 1. Attach a V-bar to a high cable pulley, stand upright facing the machine, grasp the bar with elbows at your sides. 2. Press the bar downward by extending your elbows fully, feel your triceps engage at the bottom. 3. Return to bent position with control. The V-bar provides a natural grip position for pressing.

exercises.name: Tuck Crunch
exercises.instructions: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted, place your hands behind your head or across your chest. 2. Crunch upward by lifting your shoulders off the ground, contracting your abs, hold briefly. 3. Lower back down slowly. Keep tension in your abs—avoid pulling on your neck.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a preacher bench and place your upper arms on the pad, hold a dumbbell in each hand, elbows slightly bent. 2. Curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders against the bench resistance. 3. Lower them back down under control. The preacher bench eliminates momentum and isolates your biceps.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Clean
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, kettlebells at your sides. 2. In one explosive movement, drive through your legs and pull the kettlebells upward, rotate your wrists to rack them at shoulder height. 3. Lower them back to your sides with control. This dynamic movement builds power and shoulder coordination.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Jerk
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with kettlebells at shoulder height, feet hip-width apart, core braced. 2. Dip your knees slightly then explosively extend upward, pressing the kettlebells overhead using leg drive. 3. Lower them back to shoulder height. The jerk combines power from your lower body with shoulder strength.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Military Press
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand upright with kettlebells at shoulder height, palms facing inward, feet hip-width apart. 2. Press both kettlebells overhead in a controlled motion, extend your arms fully. 3. Lower them back to shoulder height. Keep your core tight and avoid excessive lower back arch.

exercises.name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, kettlebells hanging at your sides at arm's length. 2. Row both kettlebells upward toward your hips, retract your shoulder blades and pull your elbows back. 3. Lower them back down under control. Keep your torso upright throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Underhand Cable Pulldowns
exercises.instructions: 1. Sit at a cable machine with an underhand grip on the bar, hands shoulder-width apart. 2. Pull the bar down toward your chest by squeezing your lats and driving your elbows downward. 3. Return the bar to the starting position under control. The underhand grip emphasizes your lower lats and biceps.

exercises.name: Upright Barbell Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand holding a barbell at thigh level with hands close together, feet hip-width apart. 2. Pull the barbell vertically upward, keep the bar close to your body and lead with your elbows. 3. Lower the bar back to thigh level. This compound movement targets your shoulders and traps powerfully.

exercises.name: Upright Cable Row
exercises.instructions: 1. Stand facing a cable machine at mid-height, grasp the rope or bar with hands close together. 2. Pull upward vertically, drive your elbows back and up, bring your hands toward your chin. 3. Lower back to the starting position with control. The cable provides constant tension throughout the movement.

exercises.name: Upright Row - With Bands
